fullContent:
ETH longs took $11.25M in ethereum liquidations. Spot slid to $1,745 in that same hour. Aggregated force-close tallies from Binance, Bybit, and OKX logged the wipeout through 21:20 UTC on November 19, 2026. Total liquidations on those venues reached about $11.46 million. Price fell about 1.13% from $1,764 to $1,745. Leveraged bulls cleared as Ethereum broke under $1,750.

Why Ethereum Liquidations Hit Longs First

Long liquidations were $11.25 million of the $11.46 million total. Short liquidations came to only about $210,000 on the same three venues. This means the flush hit longs almost exclusively. In other words, the window was a one-sided ethereum liquidations event, not a balanced squeeze.

Binance ETHUSDT printed the slide in the same hour. The 21:00 UTC candle opened at $1,761.20. It closed at $1,741.60 after a session low of $1,736.28. The 21:20 UTC minute close sat near $1,745.16. That print matched the $1,745 handle in the venue tally. Spot quote volume on that flush hour ran near $37 million on Binance. The Motley Fool listed Ether at $1,745.57 in its early-evening tape. The 24-hour decline was about 1.64%. This means two separate prints landed on the same sub-$1,750 zone.

The $1,764 starting print sits above the Binance hour open of $1,761.20. The $1,745 finish sits above the $1,736.28 session low. This means the ethereum liquidations clock covered the slide into $1,745. Binance still tagged a deeper wick inside the same hour. In other words, the force-close level and the deepest spot print are related but not identical.

What Traders Watch After $1,745

Binance ETHUSDT closed the 21:00 UTC hour at $1,741.60 after a flush that tagged $1,736.28. The next hour opened at that $1,741 handle. It then pushed through $1,762 by about 22:35 UTC. The bounce forced about $690,000 in short liquidations across major venues. The reclaim still held near $1,760 into the following prints.

Why the Ethereum Price Rebound Stuck

The 22:00 UTC Binance hour opened at $1,741.61 and closed at $1,760.52. The high of that hour was $1,766.39. This means buyers lifted the pair about $19 off the hour open. The print then settled just under $1,761. In other words, the move was a timed spot rebound from the $1,741 dip. It was not a slow grind across a full session. CoinGecko minute prints showed ETH near $1,762 around 22:40 UTC. That matched the same reclaim window. Later readings still sat near $1,760. About a 1.1% hourly gain remained visible on the bounce candle. The reclaim therefore stuck after the flush. It did not fade back into the $1,745 area on the first retest.

The first push was funded by the liquidation burst.

title: Trump's energy deal with Putin and Xi isn't sitting well with some Republicans
description:
Ukraine’s allies in Congress and across Europe were despondent Thursday, fearing that President Donald Trump’s latest gambit to increase global fuel supplies will weaken their effort to stop Russia’s aggression.
Their concern followed a trilateral meeting in which Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Chinese leader Xi Jinping agreed to resolutions that included increasing energy output and condemning the International Criminal Court and “and other similar bodies” that have tried to hold Russia accountable for what United Nations investigators declared last month to be war crimes in Ukraine.
Republicans in Congress called it a “big mistake” that won’t reduce fuel prices.
“They use the proceeds of their exports to fund the war to kill Ukrainian civilians,” said Texas GOP Sen. John Cornyn, who is leaving the Senate after losing his primary in May. “I think that's a big mistake, and, also, I think it's the wrong cure for the disease because it really wasn't able to really have an impact on diesel prices before the midterms.”
The White House says Trump’s intention is to help end the grinding war in Ukraine, but his critics in Congress and elsewhere see the agreement as empowering the Russian leader, who he called a “friend” at their summit in China and has frequently praised as a “genius.”
Oleksandr Merezhko, a member of the Ukrainian parliament, described the meeting as “problematic” and said the optics were “unfortunate.”
“Putin comes out ahead here, but only in terms of propaganda — there are no tangible results whatsoever,” Merezhko said.
In Congress, multiple Republicans denounced the meeting, and the four-pointjoint statement issued by the U.S., China and Russia after the summit Thursday in Shenzhen.
Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N.C.), a frequent Trump critic, said he hopes the incoming Democrats will hold the administration accountable in ways his own party didn’t.
“If anybody is going to change it, it’s going to be a Democrat majority that will use leverage and I hope they do use whatever leverage they have to rescind the waivers,” Tillis said, referring to the president’s decision to waive sections of a new law that imposed tariffs on Russian oil and gas.
Allowing a surge in Russian fuel products onto the market may end up “disincentivizing the development of refining capacity in the U.S.,” said Sen. Cynthia Lummis (R-Wyo.).
White House spokesperson Olivia Wales said Trump is advocating for more oil on the market to lower gas prices and that his dealings with Putin do not detract from his desire to end the war in Ukraine.
“President Trump is committed to achieving a lasting, just peace in Ukraine and ending the senseless killing,” she said. “The President has consistently advocated for more oil on the market to lower gas prices for American consumers; he continues to work to end the war in Ukraine while simultaneously putting America first.”
Trump’s trilateral meeting came as his special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were in Berlin, meeting with European officials to seek a way to end the war.
The president, on his way back to Washington, called into the meeting and said Putin was serious about negotiating a peace deal even as the Russian leader on Thursday denounced Ukraine’s strikes on the Crimean bridge, and vowed retaliation.
“We will not negotiate. We will respond to these attacks,” Putin said, promising a response “much more painful” than the damage to the bridge.
Still, Kushner and Witkoff, speaking after Trump’s call, insisted that peace was within reach and that the president was pushing toward that end.
“The president has adamantly supported a peaceful end to this war,” Witkoff said. “And what I heard from him on the call today, was that he mentioned these very same principles to the other two leaders he was meeting with. He made Ukraine and a peaceful end to this a principle part of that trilateral today and I think needs to be commended for that.”
The White House’s readout of the trilateral meeting didn’t mention Ukraine or a peace proposal. Nor did any of the leaders’ statements suggest that Trump pushed for an end to Putin’s aggression against Ukraine or challenged Xi’s role in supporting the conflict through exports of components essential to Moscow’s military.
John Erath, who served as National Security Council deputy director for European affairs during the first Trump administration, said the trilateral meeting was aimed at achieving a short-term price dip in world markets with little concern for the broader geopolitical consequences.
“Trump understands that an agreement — even a totally paper one — to increase energy supplies is going to have an effect on world markets and probably bring down the price of oil in the short term,” he said. “It’s geared towards the short-term movement in oil prices and what Americans pay at the pump, and I'm not sure there was much thought given for the long-term effects on Ukraine or elsewhere.”
Gas prices have fallen significantly in recent weeks. The average price for a gallon of gas is $3.72, down from $4.30 one month ago. That drop is due in part to seasonal fluctuations as well as hopes for a negotiated end to the Iran war.
On Thursday, energy markets had little reaction to the news out of the summit.
Russia has little capacity to further relieve global energy prices after Ukraine destroyed or damaged 15 of its 35 refineries in recent months. November refinery volumes were cut almost in half, Reuters reported Wednesday, causing domestic fuel shortages and forcing a cut in some exports.
U.S. officials have urged Kyiv to spare those refineries but Ukraine — and some of its European allies — have rejected stopping those strikes.
Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby visited Brussels last week and admonished Ukraine for hitting oil and gas sites inside Russia, claiming they “have not been effective … nor do they contribute to blunting Russia’s advances on the front line.”
NATO allies immediately pushed back with German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius calling Colby’s criticism “quite a stupid thing.”
Veronika Melkozerova contributed to this report.
This article originally appeared on Politico at https://www.politico.com/news/2026/11/19/trump-trilateral-backlash-republicans-ukraine-allies-01177262

title: Could Bitcoin’s March 2020 Crash Repeat?
Homeland Security Launches New Centre to Hit Crypto Scams, Cybercrime and Sextortion Networks
description: TRM Labs has been selected to supply the investigative technology for the new US government initiative targeting online scams and cybercrime.
fullContent:
The Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) has launched a Threat Disruption Center to combat cryptocurrency fraud, cybercrime, online scams, and sextortion schemes targeting Americans. The new unit will operate within the HSTF’s National Coordination Center (NCC).

The main objective is to disrupt the flow of stolen money to foreign criminal networks by bringing law enforcement agencies and private-sector companies together to act on intelligence more quickly.

Disrupting Global Scam Networks

Co-led by the Department of Homeland Security and the Department of Justice, the NCC will bring together more than 30 federal agencies and over 440 state and local partners. The center will provide investigators with shared technology to assess victim complaints, trace criminal networks, and identify their infrastructure, while establishing a channel for coordination with companies that can intervene before further losses occur.

These interventions could include pausing suspicious payments, taking down malicious websites, as well as banning social media accounts used to target victims. Companies can take such action under their own terms of service, while law enforcement continues its investigations, prosecutions and court-authorised seizures.

The initiative comes as reported losses from cybercrime continue to rise. The FBI’s Internet Crime Complaint Center recorded $20.9 billion in victim losses in 2025. This excludes people who never report being scammed, so the actual figure could be much higher. The National Center for Missing & Exploited Children, meanwhile, received an average of 137 reports of financial sextortion involving minors each day that year.

HSTF said criminal networks increasingly rely on social media, web infrastructure, banking, payment services and crypto platforms to reach victims and move illicit proceeds. The Threat Disruption Center is intended to use those same points of contact to interrupt their operations.

TRM Labs Joins Forces

TRM Labs has been selected as the newly formed entity’s primary private-sector partner to provide the technology and operational support behind its investigations. The company will deploy Ardence, its super intelligence (SI) orchestration platform, as Threat Disruption Center’s main investigative tool, in addition to dedicated engineering and investigative teams.

The platform is designed to help investigators identify different parts of criminal networks, map their infrastructure, and establish the extent of their victim base. TRM will also support the coordination of intelligence between government agencies and participating companies to enable faster responses to suspected scams and the movement of stolen funds.

title: 3 Reasons Why This AI-Related Cryptocurrency is Up 20% in a Week
description: VVV has become the 65th-biggest cryptocurrency.
fullContent:
The past week has been unkind to several leading cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), Internet Computer (ICP), Pi Network (PI), and others, which have tumbled by double digits.

However, Venice Token (VVV) defied the latest pullback and emerged as one of the top market performers. Let’s check out what could be driving the rally.

The Potential Catalysts

VVV currently trades just below $23, up approximately 20% on a weekly basis. Its market capitalization surged past $1.2 billion, making it the 65th-largest cryptocurrency.

Its substantial increase during a broader market downturn may have been partly fueled by momentum across AI tokens and renewed excitement around the sector. Recall that the space previously took a serious hit during the Nvidia drama, but the concerns have since subsided after the company posted better-than-expected financial results.

Moreover, there has been huge buzz around Anthropic’s upcoming IPO, which could have also brought the hype back. Other AI-related tokens well in green territory on a weekly scale include PEARL and PIVERSE.

The second potential driver might be Arthur Hayes’s endorsement. Earlier this week, the BitMEX co-founder claimed that VVV could be among the four tokens to explode before the AI bubble ends, setting $40 as a target.

The analytics platform Lookonchain noted that after predicting the jump, Hayes transferred more than $5 million worth of crypto, sparking speculation that he is positioning to buy.

Another spark behind the rally could be the wave of fresh project updates. Just hours ago, Venice’s team announced that Gemini 4 Neon has officially gone live on the platform. Earlier, it revealed that MAI Image 2.7 and MAI Image 2.7 Flash have also been integrated.

The Red Flags

Despite the strong rally, two key factors suggest that VVV may head south in the short term. The first one is the token’s Relative Strength Index (RSI), which has entered overbought territory at around 75. This means the price has pumped too much in a short period and could be gearing up for a pullback. The index’s ratio ranges from 0 to 100, where anything below 30 is typically interpreted as a buying opportunity.

Next on the list is the holders’ distribution. According to CoinMarketCap, the top 10 addresses control more than 90% of VVV’s circulating supply, leaving the token heavily exposed to potential market manipulation and sudden whale-driven price swings.

title: Former global sensation Fiona the hippo dies after eating a visitor's hat
description:
The Cincinnati Zoo announced Thursday that its famed hippo Fiona has died 11 days after swallowing a knit cap that slipped into her enclosure. She was nine years old.
"It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency," the zoo said in a statement.
The zoo's animal care team spent days trying to help Fiona pass the obstruction, going so far as to use a vibration plate borrowed from a horse farm to help shake it through her digestive tract. An ultrasound showed bunching in Fiona's intestines; a colonoscopy with a 9-foot scope didn't help, nor did a "giant" enema. 
“Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible,” said Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike. “We are in shock at the moment. We did not expect this outcome. She fought until she couldn’t anymore.”

It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency. https://t.co/X0GVbDAiEQ pic.twitter.com/7wLF0uclWB
— Cincinnati Zoo (@CincinnatiZoo) November 19, 2026
Specialists said surgery wasn't an option for a full-grown Nile hippopotamus. "They have a multichambered stomach for digesting plants — sort of like a cow — but they don't regurgitate and chew cud like a cow does," Jack Kottwitz, an assistant professor at Michigan State University's College of Veterinary Medicine, told the Associated Press. "Those multiple chambers, tissue folds, fluid and digesting food easily 'hide' the hat, making removal with an endoscope from the stomach chambers very difficult." 
Hippos are also difficult to anesthetize and keep away from water as they heal. 
Zoo spokesperson Michelle Curley told reporters that Fiona ingested the knit hat on Nov. 8 after it was tossed in the air by a child and flung by a ceiling fan through a 1-foot opening above the viewing windows of her enclosure. “We probably couldn't make that happen again if we tried,” Curley said at the time. “It was clearly an accident."
In the days that followed, Fiona’s appetite started to wane.
Fiona was no stranger to health struggles; she became a sensation after she was born six weeks premature in 2017. At the time, she couldn't stand on her own and weighed just 29 pounds; the next smallest Nile hippo on record weighed roughly twice as much at birth. 
No one expected Fiona to survive. Zoo staff had to bottle-feed her with a mixture of formula and her mother's milk. (A hippopotamus had never been hand-milked before.) While teething, Fiona began to refuse the bottle, and clinicians from Cincinnati Children's Hospital were called in to administer fluids intravenously. 
Fiona in 2020.
John Minchillo/AP

But eventually Fiona began to thrive. Named after Shrek's love interest, Princess Fiona — zoo staff thought her ears had a similar shape — she went on to star in her own show on YouTube and other platforms. Her plight — and her adorable triumph over adversity — inspired a host of children's books, a line of beer, a bobblehead and even a limited-edition ice cream flavor. She weighed nearly 2,500 pounds when she died. 
Fiona also became a Cincinnati icon. Her character in the Cincinnati Ballet's 2018 production of Nutcracker reportedly "stole the show"; the same year, a Fiona mural was unveiled downtown.
"Our city is heartbroken," Mayor Aftab Pureval wrote on social media, "but we couldn't be more grateful that she was part of our lives and our community as a whole."
“Our hearts are with the staff of the Cincinnati Zoo and everyone who loved her,” added outgoing Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine. “She will be deeply missed.”
Amy Acton, Ohio’s incoming governor, said that Fiona’s survival story “brought joy, hope and a little extra magic to our state.”
Second Lady Usha Vance, the wife of Vice President JD Vance, shared an undated photo of one of their children gazing at Fiona through the glass of her enclosure. “We are so sad to hear the news about Fiona,” Vance wrote. “Our family loved visiting her at the Cincinnati Zoo.”
This article originally appeared on Yahoo News at https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/article/fiona-the-hippo-dies-after-swallowing-hat-in-freak-accident-at-the-cincinnati-zoo-211146772.html

An ultrasound showed bunching in Fiona's intestines; a colonoscopy with a 9-foot scope didn't help, nor did a "giant" enema. 

“Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible,” said Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike. “We are in shock at the moment. We did not expect this outcome. She fought until she couldn’t anymore.”

It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency. https://t.co/X0GVbDAiEQ pic.twitter.com/7wLF0uclWB

— Cincinnati Zoo (@CincinnatiZoo) November 19, 2026

Specialists said surgery wasn't an option for a full-grown Nile hippopotamus. "They have a multichambered stomach for digesting plants — sort of like a cow — but they don't regurgitate and chew cud like a cow does," Jack Kottwitz, an assistant professor at Michigan State University's College of Veterinary Medicine, told the Associated Press. "Those multiple chambers, tissue folds, fluid and digesting food easily 'hide' the hat, making removal with an endoscope from the stomach chambers very difficult."

Hippos are also difficult to anesthetize and keep away from water as they heal.

Zoo spokesperson Michelle Curley told reporters that Fiona ingested the knit hat on Nov. 8 after it was tossed in the air by a child and flung by a ceiling fan through a 1-foot opening above the viewing windows of her enclosure. “We probably couldn't make that happen again if we tried,” Curley said at the time. “It was clearly an accident."

In the days that followed, Fiona’s appetite started to wane.

Fiona was no stranger to health struggles; she became a sensation after she was born six weeks premature in 2017. At the time, she couldn't stand on her own and weighed just 29 pounds; the next smallest Nile hippo on record weighed roughly twice as much at birth.

No one expected Fiona to survive. Zoo staff had to bottle-feed her with a mixture of formula and her mother's milk. (A hippopotamus had never been hand-milked before.) While teething, Fiona began to refuse the bottle, and clinicians from Cincinnati Children's Hospital were called in to administer fluids intravenously.

But eventually Fiona began to thrive. Named after Shrek's love interest, Princess Fiona — zoo staff thought her ears had a similar shape — she went on to star in her own show on YouTube and other platforms. Her plight — and her adorable triumph over adversity — inspired a host of children's books, a line of beer, a bobblehead and even a limited-edition ice cream flavor. She weighed nearly 2,500 pounds when she died.

Fiona also became a Cincinnati icon. Her character in the Cincinnati Ballet's 2018 production of Nutcracker reportedly "stole the show"; the same year, a Fiona mural was unveiled downtown.

"Our city is heartbroken," Mayor Aftab Pureval wrote on social media, "but we couldn't be more grateful that she was part of our lives and our community as a whole."

“Our hearts are with the staff of the Cincinnati Zoo and everyone who loved her,” added outgoing Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine. “She will be deeply missed.”

Amy Acton, Ohio’s incoming governor, said that Fiona’s survival story “brought joy, hope and a little extra magic to our state.”

Second Lady Usha Vance, the wife of Vice President JD Vance, shared an undated photo of one of their children gazing at Fiona through the glass of her enclosure. “We are so sad to hear the news about Fiona,” Vance wrote. “Our family loved visiting her at the Cincinnati Zoo.”

This article originally appeared on Yahoo News at https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/article/fiona-the-hippo-dies-after-swallowing-hat-in-freak-accident-at-the-cincinnati-zoo-211146772.html

title: Gold and Bitcoin Are Falling. Peter Schiff Sees Opportunities for Both
description:
Peter Schiff calls gold's drop a buying chance and Bitcoin's decline a chance to sell. Here is his case for both assets.
The post Gold and Bitcoin Are Falling. Peter Schiff Sees Opportunities for Both appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Peter Schiff says gold should not have fallen at all, while Bitcoin (BTC) has not fallen enough. The gold advocate calls the metal’s drop a buying opportunity and Bitcoin’s a selling opportunity.

Both assets have dropped, yet Schiff’s reading gives their holders opposite instructions. Gold’s decline is a discount to buy, in his view, while Bitcoin’s is still a window to leave. This is an expected response from the famously anti-Bitcoin gold bug.

Why Does Peter Schiff Read the Same Selloff in Opposite Ways?

Schiff, a longtime gold advocate and Bitcoin critic, argues that gold should not have fallen at all.

In his view, that turns the drop into a discount rather than a warning.

Bitcoin, by contrast, has not fallen far enough in Schiff’s view. That leaves room for more losses and makes current levels an exit rather than an entry.

He has argued for rotating out of Bitcoin before, including a call to sell Bitcoin as gold rallied.

Has Bitcoin Followed the Script Schiff Expected?

Schiff has not always seen Bitcoin fall on schedule.

Gold and Bitcoin both rallied after U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced plans to roughly double the government’s bond buybacks.

Gold later surrendered that rally, while Bitcoin kept its gains. That surprised Schiff, according to a Moneywise report on his remarks on The Wolf of All Streets podcast.

However, he had expected a fall by now and still predicts new lows. He also argued that Washington is likelier to be an enemy than a friend to Bitcoin in the coming months.

Schiff further suggested part of Bitcoin’s run-up came from the technology rally that lifted large-cap stocks. Under that reading, a fading tech rally could pull Bitcoin lower.

Underneath sits a wider question. Does Bitcoin act as a hedge like gold, or as a risk asset tied to equities?

A tech-led recovery that lifts Bitcoin while gold stays weak would undercut his sell call.

The post Gold and Bitcoin Are Falling. Peter Schiff Sees Opportunities for Both appeared first on BeInCrypto.

title: Almost all of Anthropic's employees are now millionaires
description:
Anthropic captured a $1.76 trillion valuation on its first day of trading on the Nasdaq. - Mike Segar/Reuters
Anthropic’s stock market debut turned the vast majority of the young startup’s staff into overnight millionaires — some many times over.
The company’s headcount stood at 5,300 as of September this year, according to regulatory filings. After Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, about 600 employees entered the rarefied “centi-millionaire” club, with equity holdings valued north of $100 million, according to data from Hill.com, which tracks private-company shares.
As many as 2,800 staffers, known internally as “Ants,” have holdings valued above $10 million. And about 5,100 — 96% of the staff — are sitting on equity north of $1 million.
“What’s most surprising here is how quickly this this happened,” Andrew Benson, Hill’s founder and CEO, told CNN on Thursday, noting Anthropic has seen very little attrition. “It’s been pretty clear for some time that Anthropic is a rocket ship, and so it definitely discouraged people from leaving because they knew what the opportunity cost of that would be.”
It’s not unusual for Silicon Valley startups, which are typically light on cash, to pay their staff with a combination of salary and stock. The promise of a future acquisition or initial public offering tends to keep workers motivated to work hard and stick it out until payday.
But few startups have grown as big or as quickly as Anthropic. The company, founded in 2021, had fewer than 1,000 employees at the end of 2024.
As with most tech startups, Benson noted, “being early is more important, in terms of a financial outcome, than being senior … You could be very low on the totem pole, and if you joined in 2023 or 2024, you’re likely to have a significantly better outcome than a senior person who joined earlier this year.”
SpaceX, by contrast, spent more than two decades as a private company before its blockbuster IPO in June. That debut minted around 4,400 millionaires, out of a staff of 22,000.
unknown content item
 -
                
Anthropic’s IPO is also unique for allowing non-founder insiders to cash out on Day One of trading. In most IPOs, staff are subject to a “lockup” period — typically three to six months — during which they can’t sell their shares. But Anthropic’s listing included a complex, staggered lockup schedule that allowed non-founder insiders to cash out up to 10% of their shares as soon as the stock began trading. (It’s not known how many insiders may have taken advantage of the opportunity Thursday.)
And unlike SpaceX, which has employees spread across Texas, California and Florida, Anthropic is uniquely concentrated in San Francisco, a city whose entire economy has been reshaped by sudden surges of tech wealth.
A rash of newly minted millionaires could soon amplify pressure on San Francisco’s housing market, where home prices are already rising at their fastest pace in years.
The typical home there sold for $1.7 million in October, up nearly 19% from a year earlier, according to Redfin. By contrast, the national median home price was roughly flat over the same period, at $416,700, according to the National Association of Realtors.

CNN’s Samantha Delouya contributed reporting.

title: Solana Announces 2027 Roadmap With On-Chain AI and Faster Blocks
description:
Solana has laid out an ambitious technical roadmap for 2027. Anza CEO Brennan Watt unveiled the plan at Breakpoint 2026, building on October’s Alpenglow upgrade. However, SOL has struggled this year. Can the network’s upgrades finally turn the token’s fortunes around? Inside Solana’s Four-Pillar Roadmap for 2027 Solana’s 2027 roadmap follows a major 2026 milestone.
The post Solana Announces 2027 Roadmap With On-Chain AI and Faster Blocks appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
Solana has laid out an ambitious technical roadmap for 2027. Anza CEO Brennan Watt unveiled the plan at Breakpoint 2026, building on October’s Alpenglow upgrade.

However, SOL has struggled this year. Can the network’s upgrades finally turn the token’s fortunes around?

Inside Solana’s Four-Pillar Roadmap for 2027

Solana’s 2027 roadmap follows a major 2026 milestone. Alpenglow, which went live on October 21, cut transaction finality from about 12.8 seconds to roughly 150 milliseconds. Solana also left its long “mainnet beta” phase.

For 2027, the roadmap focuses on these four areas:

  • Performance: Doubling compute capacity from about 250 million to 500 million units per second, while cutting token-account transaction costs by 80%.
  • Expressivity: Adding native vector processing so AI models can run fully on-chain, and raising the accounts-per-transaction limit from 64 to 96.
  • Market structure: Introducing Rotor, a faster replacement for Turbine, and Constellation, which sets clearer transaction ordering rules.
  • Resilience: Simplifying the protocol, removing special cases, and making future upgrades safer and faster to deploy.

Together, these changes aim to strengthen Solana’s position in DeFi, high-throughput apps, and emerging on-chain AI use cases.

Can SOL Price Recover After a 40% Drop This Year?

Not necessarily, at least in the short term. According to BeInCrypto data, SOL trades near $73.7, up roughly 0.5% over the past 24 hours.

The broader picture looks far weaker. SOL opened 2026 around $124 and reached a yearly high near $148 in mid-January. It then bottomed near $60 in June.

Since the start of the year, the token has dropped roughly 40%. It has also lost about 30% over the past 30 days alone. Moreover, SOL sits about 75% below its $293 all-time high from January 2025.

However, a lasting rally will depend on whether the roadmap delivers measurable growth in usage. Broader market conditions and macroeconomic factors will also shape SOL’s path next year.

The post Solana Announces 2027 Roadmap With On-Chain AI and Faster Blocks appeared first on BeInCrypto.

fullContent:
WASHINGTON—In a change of designation that marks a major step backward in the effort to curb rowdy youth subcultures, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) announced Wednesday that the United States had officially lost its greaser elimination status. “Following significant upticks in the number of defiant teens sporting slicked-back hair, leather biker jackets, and cuffed blue jeans, we must regretfully remove the U.S. from our list of greaser-free countries,” PAHO director Dr. Jarbas Barbosa said in a public statement, explaining that what began with the isolated incident of a sock hop in West Texas had rapidly grown into a nationwide epidemic. “Unfortunately, as more parents have declined to raise their children to be clean-cut, the greaser infestation continues to spread undeterred through our high schools, drive-in theaters, malt shops, and vacant parking lots. Not since the rockabilly revival of the early 1980s have Americans been exposed to these staggering levels of pomade and Brylcreem. We fought long and hard to eradicate chain-smoking, finger-snapping delinquents in our country, and it will likely take decades of work to get them back under control. We urge officials to contain the outbreak by enforcing strict public dress codes and anti-loitering laws as soon as possible.” Barbosa went on to warn that if the United States continued down its current path, it could soon see a resurgence of beatniks.

title: Bitcoin Is No Longer as Risky as It Was a Decade Ago: Grayscale
description:
Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) is becoming a more mature investment asset, with declining volatility, improving diversification benefits and return patterns that challenge traditional measures of risk, according to a new Grayscale report.
While Bitcoin has experienced seven drawdowns exceeding 50% since 2011, the declines appear less extreme when adjusted for Bitcoin’s underlying volatility.
The report “Beyond Volatility: Rethinking Crypto Risk” noted that Bitcoin’s annualized realized volatility has declined from peaks approaching 200% in its early years to roughly 43-45% today.
Its volatility is also lower than that of almost 19% of S&P 500 constituents, including several large-cap stocks.
The shift is attributed to growing institutional participation, more secure investment vehicles like exchange-traded products (ETPs), deeper liquidity, and greater regulatory clarity.
Grayscale also explained that Bitcoin no longer explains the entire cryptocurrency market’s performance.
Over the past three years, Bitcoin accounted for only about 50% of the variation in crypto sector returns, suggesting that individual sectors increasingly respond to distinct catalysts.
Among the 10 largest cryptocurrencies excluding stablecoins, six different assets led quarterly performance over the past two years. Bitcoin did not lead in any quarter.
Can BTC Improve Portfolio Returns?
Grayscale highlighted Bitcoin’s diversification potential, citing JPMorgan Asset Management’s projections of 10% annualized returns, 55% volatility and just 33% correlation with U.S. large-cap stocks over the next decade.
JPMorgan expects Bitcoin to outperform other major asset classes.
Grayscale’s back testing found that modest Bitcoin allocations improved portfolio returns and Sharpe ratios without proportionately increasing volatility or drawdowns.
Image: Shutterstock

title: Zoomex Review 2026: Crypto, Stocks, AI Tools, and Savings Under One Platform
description:
If you keep USDT on a crypto exchange, there’s a practical reason to look at Zoomex. You can use that balance to buy Bitcoin, trade the price of gold, or earn interest while you decide what to do with it. The appeal is clearest if you already trade across markets. Zoomex lists the United States
The post Zoomex Review 2026: Crypto, Stocks, AI Tools, and Savings Under One Platform appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
If you keep USDT on a crypto exchange, there’s a practical reason to look at Zoomex. You can use that balance to buy Bitcoin, trade the price of gold, or earn interest while you decide what to do with it. The appeal is clearest if you already trade across markets.

Zoomex lists the United States and the European Union among its excluded markets. For readers who can use it, here’s how the platform fits together.

Zoomex Crypto Trading Accounts

The simplest place to start is spot trading. If you spend $100 on Bitcoin, you hold the amount of BTC that $100 buys after fees. You can leave it on the exchange or withdraw it to your own wallet.

There’s much more choice in futures. On November 18, CoinGecko tracked 69 Zoomex spot pairs and 737 derivatives pairs. A perpetual futures contract lets you trade on whether a price will rise or fall. It has no expiry, and you can lose the money backing your position if the market moves far enough against you.

Zoomex’s trading account handles both markets. If you trade futures, one setting deserves attention before your first order.

  • Isolated margin sets aside collateral for one position. It’s the easier choice for understanding how much of your balance backs that trade.
  • Cross margin lets positions draw on a shared pool of eligible assets. That’s convenient for an experienced trader managing several positions. It also means one losing trade can eat into funds backing another.

Note: One small inconvenience shows up when you want to cash out. Zoomex asks you to move crypto back to your Funding Account before withdrawing it. 

KYC Requirements

Zoomex generally lets you trade crypto without verifying your identity. It requires verification if you want to withdraw more than the equivalent of 100 BTC in a day, and it may also ask for ID during a security or compliance review. 

If you buy crypto with a card or another fiat payment method, the payment provider may also require its own identity check.

How Much a Trade Costs on Zoomex

Zoomex’s standard fees are close to those of other large exchanges. A maker leaves an order on the book for someone else to fill. A taker accepts an available price, as you usually do with a market order.

Assumes a $1,000 trade in each direction at the same price. The figures exclude the gap between buy and sell prices. Perpetual traders may also pay or receive funding while a position stays open.

With leverage, fees apply to the full position. Put up $100 to control $1,000, and that $1.20 round trip uses 1.2% of your starting money. Frequent traders can qualify for lower rates through the VIP program.

Zoomex TradFi Review: Tokenized Stocks and Gold

The TradFi section puts familiar names on a crypto trading screen. Check the instrument before placing an order.

The practical advantage is being able to act when the underlying stock market is closed. The drawback shows up at the same time. 

Fewer orders may be available, so check the gap between the quoted buy and sell prices before trading after hours.

Note: After-hours trading depends on the rules for each contract. Some contracts switch to reduce-only when the underlying market is closed. 

AI Trading Features

Zoomex offers several ways to get help with a trade. What matters is who makes the next decision.

  • AI trading assistant. Connect a compatible AI assistant and you can ask what positions you hold or how close one is to liquidation. Zoomex also shows an example where the assistant prepares an order for approval. Its public directory lists account and market queries as live. We couldn’t verify live order submission through the assistant.
  • Strategy Center and grid bots. Pick a price range and a bot places futures orders as the market moves through it. A grid can show profits on completed trades while its open position loses money. Look at the total return. Zoomex lists its recommended presets as web-only.
  • Copy trading. Choose a trader and allocate USDT in a separate copy account. Your orders can fill at different prices from theirs. Zoomex’s follower guide also describes a 10% deduction from net profits for profit sharing.

Savings, New tokens and Prediction markets

Savings gives idle crypto a use. Flexible savings lets you redeem when you need the funds. Fixed savings locks them until maturity.

Note: Users must read the Earn terms before choosing based on the advertised rate alone. Zoomex can pool deposits and decide how to use them to generate yield. The return can change.

Launchpad serves a different purpose. You commit USDT for a chance to buy a new token. That money is unavailable for trading or withdrawal while the commitment lasts.

The prediction market lets you take a position on an event outcome. You can request an early sale, though getting out depends on available buyers. If you hold to the end, check which source decides the result.

Under the settlement rules, a disputed outcome can delay payment.

Should You Consider Zoomex as Your Main Investment App?

For an active trader who already keeps funds in USDT, Zoomex makes a good case. The shared trading account is its best feature. 

You can move between crypto and traditional-market contracts without funding a second platform. For a beginner, spot is the easiest part to use and understand. A long-term investor who wants direct ownership of shares has less reason to move here.

Putting more money on one exchange also makes custody more important. Zoomex publishes reserve wallet information, and Hacken has tested its web application.

title: California attorney general opens probe into Nvidia over Jensen Huang scandal
description:
California Attorney General Rob Bonta is launching an investigation into Nvidia following revelations of former CEO Jensen Huang’s reported affair with a woman U.S. intelligence officials have accused of being a Chinese spy
“We’re specifically investigating whether Nvidia’s advanced chips or their confidential information may have gone to China and whether Nvidia misled investors and the public,” Bonta told POLITICO on Thursday.
Nvidia's chips are a key component of powerful AI models, making them highly valuable to tech companies jockeying for a leg up in the race to develop new iterations of the technology. Officials in Washington have sought to prevent China from obtaining the company’s most advanced chips through export controls.
Bonta told POLITICO an investigative subpoena his office served on Nvidia Thursday is the first step in its investigation into whether the company violated state law, saying other subpoenas might be warranted depending on the information his office receives from the company.
“We expect cooperation,” he added. “Doesn’t mean they will, but unless and until they don’t comply, I expect compliance.”
Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment.
The Wall Street Journal reported earlier this week that the Securities and Exchange Commission has opened its own investigation into Nvidia, probing whether the company’s financial disclosures misled investors. POLITICO has not confirmed the SEC investigation.
“There is clear law in California, corporate securities law in California, that makes it very certain that companies cannot mislead their investors, whether it’s in public statements, statements to reporters or statements to the SEC,” Bonta said.
Huang has been a regular presence in Washington, using his close relationship with President Donald Trump to lobby against efforts aimed at restricting semiconductor exports to China. Bonta said he is concerned that Huang’s closeness to Trump might cause the administration to go easy on Nvidia.
“I’m not convinced [Trump] is going to take appropriate steps here with Mr. Huang,” Bonta said.
Huang’s resignation as Nvidia CEO last week has complicated tech industry lobbyists’ efforts to fend off export controls and emboldened China hawks on Capitol Hill to pursue tighter restrictions on chip sales.
Although Huang has acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife, he has not confirmed widespread allegations he had an affair with Alice Huang while she was an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center company that was a major Nvidia customer. The significance of the relationship went far beyond an allegation of infidelity when it was revealed that U.S. officials suspected the Megaspeed exec, who is not related to Huang, of working for the Chinese government.
Bonta seemingly previewed his probe Tuesday, when he told Bloomberg that the Huang scandal raised “red flags” about Nvidia’s actions and was “very possibly” something his office would investigate.
This article originally appeared on Politico at https://www.politico.com/news/2026/11/19/rob-bonta-probes-nvidia-over-jensen-huang-scandal-01177017

title: Is Tech in a Bear Market? 20 Tech Stocks Fall Up to 76% From Highs
description:
Kobeissi Letter data shows 20 tech stocks down 25% to 76% from record highs as the S&P 500 sheds over $6 trillion.
The post Is Tech in a Bear Market? 20 Tech Stocks Fall Up to 76% From Highs appeared first on BeInCrypto.
fullContent:
All 20 tech stocks on a list from financial newsletter The Kobeissi Letter trade at least 25% below record highs. CoreWeave (CRWV) leads the slide at 76%.

Additionally, the S&P 500 has lost over $6 trillion in six weeks adding pressure to the markets in general. The Nasdaq Composite, however, sits in correction territory, a 10% decline, not the 20% that defines a bear market.

Why Are Cloud and Chip Names Falling Hardest?

The deepest drops cluster in cloud computing, chips, and data storage. Oracle (ORCL) and SanDisk (SNDK), a flash memory maker, each trail their highs by 68%. Nebius (NBIS), an artificial intelligence (AI) cloud provider, is down 66%.

Source: The Kobeissi Letter

Intel (INTC) is down 61%. Western Digital (WDC), a data storage maker, and Arm (ARM), a chip designer, each trail by 60%. Tesla (TSLA) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) show the mildest declines at 25%, still beyond the 20% bear market line.

CoreWeave, which rents computing capacity to AI developers, grew third-quarter revenue 168% to $3.66 billion. Its net loss still reached $709 million, with net interest expense at $846 million, according to its results.

A correction means a 10% decline from a record, while a bear market requires 20%. The Nasdaq Composite closed at 23,879.20 on Nov. 19. That sits below the 24,315.00 close that confirmed its correction on Nov. 5, CNBC reported.

Meanwhile, the S&P 500 fell 2.02% on Nov. 19 to 7,175.83. AMD fell further after short seller Hunterbrook Capital disclosed a bet against the chipmaker.

Will the Indexes Follow These Tech Stocks Lower?

The Kobeissi Letter, meanwhile, has described the selloff as a historic opportunity. In both earlier 2026 episodes, in March and July, the Composite later set new records, a Motley Fool analysis shows.

If that pattern holds, indexes could recover while these 20 stocks lag. A close 20% below the Oct. 6 record, however, would most likely break it.

title: Inside Bukele’s Casa Presidencial Dinner: Bitcoiners Discuss Energy, Immigration, and El Salvador’s Future
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Inside Bukele’s Casa Presidencial Dinner: Bitcoiners Discuss Energy, Immigration, and El Salvador’s Future
On November 10, 2026, President Nayib Bukele hosted roughly 30 Bitcoiners at Casa Presidencial during Bitcoin Histórico. Guests included Ricardo Salinas Pliego, Parker Lewis, Mike Peterson, and miners; discussions covered power generation for compute and immigration.
This post Inside Bukele’s Casa Presidencial Dinner: Bitcoiners Discuss Energy, Immigration, and El Salvador’s Future first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Juan Galt.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Inside Bukele’s Casa Presidencial Dinner: Bitcoiners Discuss Energy, Immigration, and El Salvador’s Future

This November 10, in the midst of the Bitcoin Histórico conference taking place in the Historical Center of San Salvador, a group of Bitcoiners representing a wide range of sectors within the industry met with President Bukele.

The dinner was organized by The Bitcoin Office, which is part of the Office of the President, and was led by Stacy Herbert and Max Keiser. The dinner went on from about 7:30 pm to 10:30 pm local time and included about thirty Bitcoiners, many regular visitors to El Salvador. 

Among the guests was billionaire Ricardo Salinas Pliego, founder of Grupo Salinas, which owns Banco Azteca. Salinas is a known Bitcoiner, who has made public appearances with Keiser and Herbert in the past, and is speculated to be planning a run at the next Mexican Presidential election. Salinas met privately with the President besides the dinner and reportedly gifted him volumes one and two of Manuscripts of the Conquistadors, works curated and edited by Jorge Nikaido, Chief of Staff of Grupo Salinas.

Representing investors and founders were Parker Lewis, founder of Unchained Capital, Mike Peterson of Bitcoin Beach fame, Katie Ananina of Citizen X, and Aleks Svetski, entrepreneur and founder of Satlantis. Bitcoin miners also attended, such as  Beau Turner,  CEO of  Abundant Mines, Nacho Pauls, CCO of OCEAN Mining, and Adam Ortolf of Denver Bitcoin mining. Jon Atack, a Bitcoin core contributor, was also at the dinner alongside engineer Giacomo Zucco of Plan B Network, and AI tech entrepreneurs Ginger Gaetz of the ANIA AI initiative and Marc Seal, Founder of Aevonix.

The academic and media side of the industry was also heavily represented, with none other than Michael Goldstein, also known as Bitstein and co-founder of the Nakamoto Institute. Eric Yakes, economist and author of The 7th Property, was there, as well as Efrat Feningson, independent journalist and podcaster. Local Bitcoiner Michael Ruiz also attended the dinner; he is the founder of Build in El Salvador (BIS), an increasingly popular kind of business club and Bitcoin meetup mix. 

Setting the Table

The guests arrived at the Casa Presidencial earlier in the evening and were chatting and networking while waiting for the president. Max Keiser, always a showman, arrived at the Casa Presidencial with a gift some might speculate carried a magical artefact. Photographed above, the case was said to contain a Stetson El Presidente cowboy hat, though some have speculated it might in fact have carried the Philosopher’s Stone. 

Upon arrival, Bukele shook everyone’s hand and quickly invited them to take their assigned seats, dine, and relax- no big speeches or over-the-top formalities, Ananina told Bitcoin Magazine, describing the dinner as a kind of open mic. 

“President Bukele’s table was adorned with bitcoin orange florals,” Herbert told Bitcoin Magazine; “we gathered anarchists, billionaire tycoons, Wall Street bankers, circular economy activists, VC investors, bitcoin miners, and content creators” at the country’s equivalent of the White House.  

A three-course meal began to be served, with steak — of course — being the main course, followed by a three-layered chocolate dessert. In between were three hours of conversation which left a very strong impression on the individuals interviewed on the night. Bukele had his own microphone, while a couple of other mics were passed around. Six to seven major questions were asked throughout the night.

Salinas and Energy Investments

At some point, energy generation came up, and Salinas in particular engaged the topic with the President. 

Baeu Turner, one of the three bitcoin miners at the dinner, told Bitcoin Magazine that Bukele described El Salvador’s electricity generation as “being roughly matched to the country’s current demand.” Bukele described plans to add more than a gigawatt of additional generation across multiple projects, including geothermal and generation using imported liquefied natural gas.

“What stood out to me,” added Turner, “was how directly he connected those development plans with demand for compute. Bukele said they can develop this power knowing there are users who can put it to work, whether that’s Bitcoin mining or other data centers. The demand could come from the Salvadoran government’s own operations or from outside companies bringing equipment and investment into the country.”

Other miners responded positively to that idea, including Salinas, who has deep investments and experience with energy production. His Grupo Dragón is involved in geothermal, wind, solar, and natural-gas generation across Mexico. 

Immigration and Gentrification

Immigration was also discussed. Spurred by Max Keiser’s enthusiasm about the country, where he roughly said that the world should recognize El Salvador’s arc and that people — bitcoiners presumably — should migrate; suddenly the topic was set on the table. Ruiz, whose family is from the region but was born and raised in the U.S., moved to El Salvador three years ago and has become a recognizable figure in the local Bitcoin community. He followed up with a question about immigration, in particular about gentrification and possible resentment from the local population towards Western migrants, pointing to very negative online comments about some Bitcoiners, such as being called “colonizers”.

Bukele asked back, “When you go out, walk around, and interact with Salvadorans, what are the interactions like?”, The question, to anyone that’s spent time in El Salvador in recent years, answers itself. Salvadorians are very welcoming, Ruiz told Bitcoin Magazine; “there’s a lot of love. People receive us with open arms, and they’re glad we’re here, and they’re happy”. 

Immigration in El Salvador actually tends to be from regional countries like Honduras, Nicaragua, Guatemala, and Colombia, with smaller numbers reported from the United States. Bukele went on to dismiss concerns about immigration, joking that you could host the whole population of the world in El Salvador by matching the population density of Manhattan. This was not a statement meant to be taken as a goal or ideal, but rather to set the topic in context. He added that the country is obviously looking for the most capable and intelligent people, and even said that “all great empires were built with immigrants’ help”, which says a lot about the President’s mindset on the topic.

In response to concerns about gentrification, the President told the story of a fisherman and house caretaker who got a raise from $300 to $800 a month from an American who bought the property. As a result, the fisherman was able to buy a motor for his boat, which he used to fish and row by hand before that. The scale-up of his fishing business was so productive that the caretaker even got his son a boat, doubling his fishing fleet. The only people who complained about this growth in wages were the neighbours, so the story goes, who must have been feeling the pressure from their own villa’s caretakers, wanting a raise from meager wages. 

Among other Topics

At some point Efrat asked, “How come you are criticized around the world despite El Salvador’s GDP growth, a strengthening economy and popularity at home, which I saw firsthand talking to locals and visiting some of the areas once worst hit by gang violence?”

“Because I’m not part of their club,” the President allegedly responded, “I’m not the kind of ruler they like”. He added that there are evil people in the world who use mainstream media to criticize leaders like him and “call him names”, central bankers, including the ECB, came up as one of the forces behind the negative media campaign against Bukele.

Beyond the clear hit pieces, he noted that many people in governments or the international political establishment are not evil per se, but are often ‘order followers’, who operate on certain narratives and resist new paradigms. 

The recent wins for the country in terms of education reform were also discussed. Bukele allegedly said that many private schools are now integrating similar AI tutoring programs as the one led by his administration. The results made international news when the pilot program deployed in public schools over the past couple of years brought PISA test results to par with Germany and Switzerland.

Renaissance 2.0

When asked about their reflections on the presidential dinner and the Bitcoin Histórico conference in general, Max Kaiser shared his vision in a manner that merits being printed in full:

“Bitcoin Histórico promised two days of Excellence Only, as the Bitcoin Office likes to say, and it delivered big time. The National Palace was a regal setting to showcase the Renaissance 2.0 taking shape in El Salvador with presentations by the best Bitcoin minds and builders in the world. Audience members felt like they had been transported to a time and place found nowhere else in the world right now, where hope and happiness are in abundance. No doom.”

Stacy Herbert, whose presence and attention to detail were felt throughout the festivities, told Bitcoin Magazine, “We promoted Bitcoin Histórico as an elevated bitcoin conference experience with Philosopher King meets Renaissance 2.0 vibes. In every detail, my team and I achieved that, including with the official Bitcoin Office dinner at Casa Presidencial.” She added that guests were free to ask any question they wanted, and that no topic was off limits. 

“They grilled the President for several hours. His wit, his charm, his intelligence – all unscripted – was there for all to see firsthand. And they will have walked away understanding why it is that El Salvador is winning under his leadership.” Herbert added. As far as attendees to the dinner who Bitcoin Magazine spoke with, both claims remain very much corroborated.

This post Inside Bukele’s Casa Presidencial Dinner: Bitcoiners Discuss Energy, Immigration, and El Salvador’s Future first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Juan Galt.

In response to concerns about gentrification, the President told the story of a fisherman and house caretaker who got a raise from $300 to $800 a month from an American who bought the property. As a result, the fisherman was able to buy a motor for his boat, which he used to fish and row by hand before that. The scale-up of his fishing business was so productive that the caretaker even got his son a boat, doubling his fishing fleet. The only people who complained about this growth in wages were the neighbours, so the story goes, who must have been feeling the pressure from their own villa’s caretakers, wanting a raise from meager wages. 

Among other Topics

At some point Efrat asked, “How come you are criticized around the world despite El Salvador’s GDP growth, a strengthening economy and popularity at home, which I saw firsthand talking to locals and visiting some of the areas once worst hit by gang violence?”

“Because I’m not part of their club,” the President allegedly responded, “I’m not the kind of ruler they like”. He added that there are evil people in the world who use mainstream media to criticize leaders like him and “call him names”, central bankers, including the ECB, came up as one of the forces behind the negative media campaign against Bukele.

Beyond the clear hit pieces, he noted that many people in governments or the international political establishment are not evil per se, but are often ‘order followers’, who operate on certain narratives and resist new paradigms. 

The recent wins for the country in terms of education reform were also discussed. Bukele allegedly said that many private schools are now integrating similar AI tutoring programs as the one led by his administration. The results made international news when the pilot program deployed in public schools over the past couple of years brought PISA test results to par with Germany and Switzerland.

Renaissance 2.0

When asked about their reflections on the presidential dinner and the Bitcoin Histórico conference in general, Max Kaiser shared his vision in a manner that merits being printed in full:

“Bitcoin Histórico promised two days of Excellence Only, as the Bitcoin Office likes to say, and it delivered big time. The National Palace was a regal setting to showcase the Renaissance 2.0 taking shape in El Salvador with presentations by the best Bitcoin minds and builders in the world. Audience members felt like they had been transported to a time and place found nowhere else in the world right now, where hope and happiness are in abundance. No doom.”

Stacy Herbert, whose presence and attention to detail were felt throughout the festivities, told Bitcoin Magazine, “We promoted Bitcoin Histórico as an elevated bitcoin conference experience with Philosopher King meets Renaissance 2.0 vibes. In every detail, my team and I achieved that, including with the official Bitcoin Office dinner at Casa Presidencial.” She added that guests were free to ask any question they wanted, and that no topic was off limits. 

“They grilled the President for several hours. His wit, his charm, his intelligence – all unscripted – was there for all to see firsthand. And they will have walked away understanding why it is that El Salvador is winning under his leadership.” Herbert added. As far as attendees to the dinner who Bitcoin Magazine spoke with, both claims remain very much corroborated.

This post Inside Bukele’s Casa Presidencial Dinner: Bitcoiners Discuss Energy, Immigration, and El Salvador’s Future first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Juan Galt.

title: Bitcoin Price Retests $61,500 – Same Zone It Lost in June
description:
Bitcoin has dropped from near $87,380 to $61,550, cutting through its daily moving averages and Fibonacci supports before landing on […]
The post Bitcoin Price Retests $61,500 – Same Zone It Lost in June appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Bitcoin has dropped from near $87,380 to $61,550, cutting through its daily moving averages and Fibonacci supports before landing on the zone where it turned repeatedly in June and July.

Key Takeaways

  • Price sits on June-July demand near $61,500
  • Daily RSI at 19.93, deep in oversold
  • Price trades 15% below 200-day SMA
  • Thursday’s high stalled just below $64,115

Whether that zone holds again is the main question on the BTCUSDT daily chart, after it gave way once in late June and then held through the summer.

Four Fibonacci Levels Gone in November

The retracement grid runs from the late-June low near $57,780 to the September peak near $87,380. Price slipped under the rising dashed trendline from that low in late October, and the November selloff then ran through four retracement levels in turn.

The 0.382 level near $76,070 went first. The 0.5 retracement near $72,580 followed on heavy red candles, and losing it cost two supports at once: the 200-day simple moving average sits close to $72,690, almost on top of it. The 0.618 level near $69,090 barely slowed the decline. Only the 0.786 level near $64,115 produced a pause, a brief bounce before sellers returned.

The 50-day SMA at $78,230 is rolling over sharply, and the 100-day at $77,760 is flattening just beneath it. With the 200-day at $72,690, price now trades about 15% below the slowest of the three averages.

Where Thursday’s Session Stalled

The session opened at $63,060, already below the 0.786 level near $64,115. It rose to $64,080, about $35 short of that line, then turned lower to $61,430. A close near current prices would mean the level that supported the mid-November bounce has now turned price away from below.

The drop brought Bitcoin to the lower edge of the blue horizontal band between roughly $61,500 and $62,300. The band caught the early-June selloff, gave way in late June, when price fell to near $57,780, and was back above it within days. Through July and into mid-August, it absorbed several pullbacks before the breakout toward $76,000. Thursday’s low dipped under $61,500 but stayed above $61,400.

What Oversold Meant Last Time

Daily RSI (14) reads 19.93, well below its own 28.96 average, which shows how far and how fast price has fallen. A reading this low does not mark a bottom by itself.

Early June offers a test case on this chart. RSI dropped deep into oversold territory then too, and price rebounded briefly before breaking below the blue band to the late-June low. An oversold reading can come before a relief rally or only interrupt a decline. In June, it was the second.

What would change the picture on the daily chart:

If the floor holds

Daily closes inside or above the $61,500 zone, with RSI turning up from 19.93, would leave room for a short-covering bounce toward the 0.786 level near $64,115. A stronger relief move would meet the 0.618 retracement near $69,090.

If $61,400 gives way

A decisive daily close below $61,400 would remove the last horizontal buffer above the range floor, leaving the 1.0 Fibonacci level and late-June low near $57,780 as the next reference.

Trend check: a bounce stays counter-trend until price reclaims the level near $64,115 and then the one near $69,090. Both still sit below the 200-day SMA at $72,690 and the 0.5 level near $72,580.

The $61,500 area carries more weight on a bigger chart. Coindoo’s monthly Bitcoin chart analysis traces it to the 2021 double top and the floor of the 2024 range, with the 0.5 Fibonacci retracement near $63,160 just above it. On that timeframe, the November close relative to $61,500 is also the test that matters.

The levels and scenarios described are based on technical analysis of the daily chart and are not predictions of future price movement. Cryptocurrency markets are highly volatile; always do your own research before making any investment decisions.

fullContent:
Privacy coins are poised to be among the biggest cryptocurrency stories of 2027, driven by growing concerns over financial surveillance, institutional adoption, and the future of digital privacy. This creates a compelling investment narrative. Google Gemini AI predicts that two projects, Monero (XMR) and Zcash (ZEC), will stand out, and it aims to forecast which will experience a significant price surge in 2027.

Both Monero and Zcash are established leaders in the privacy-focused cryptocurrency space, but they employ fundamentally different approaches to protecting users’ financial information. Monero offers privacy by default, while Zcash seeks to balance financial confidentiality with greater accessibility for institutional investors.

As a potential major crypto bull market approaches in 2027, investors may find two distinct opportunities for substantial returns. However, determining which option could deliver the biggest gains may yield surprising results.

Monero vs. Zcash: Two Different Approaches to Privacy

Monero has long been considered the gold standard for transaction privacy. Unlike conventional cryptocurrencies, where transactions can be publicly inspected on a blockchain, XMR makes privacy an inherent feature of its network.

It achieves this through ring signatures, Ring Confidential Transactions (RingCT), and stealth addresses, which conceal the sender, transaction amount, and recipient. Importantly, privacy is mandatory, not optional.

This gives Monero a compelling proposition as a digital cash alternative, especially as blockchain analytics grow more sophisticated and financial surveillance expands.

However, that same characteristic creates a significant obstacle: regulatory scrutiny. Exchanges in several jurisdictions have restricted or removed XMR trading, potentially limiting access to a broader pool of investors.

Zcash takes a different approach, using zero-knowledge cryptography to enable shielded transactions while retaining the option of transparent transactions.

Its shielded addresses let users conceal transaction details, while viewing keys let them selectively disclose information to auditors or other authorized parties. This flexibility could prove particularly attractive to institutions that want privacy without completely sacrificing compliance.

The distinction could become increasingly important as institutional investors look beyond Bitcoin and Ethereum for opportunities in specialized crypto sectors.

Gemini AI Predicts a Privacy Boom: Could Institutional Adoption Drive the Next Rally?

Privacy coins are already attracting attention beyond their traditional communities. Zcash has made considerable progress in positioning itself as a more institutionally accessible privacy network, with regulated investment products emerging and interest in its underlying technology growing.

Meanwhile, Monero continues to benefit from its established reputation, consistent privacy guarantees and decentralized architecture.

The broader investment narrative is also changing. As cryptocurrency adoption increases, more transactions become visible to blockchain analytics companies, incentivizing individuals and businesses to seek greater financial confidentiality.

However, the regulatory landscape could become a major obstacle in 2027. The EU’s Anti-Money Laundering Regulation is scheduled to apply from July 10, 2027, with restrictions covering crypto-asset accounts involving anonymity-enhancing coins.

Crucially, the legislation’s definition encompasses privacy features that operate either systematically or optionally. This means neither project can assume its architecture provides an exemption.

XMR vs. ZEC: What Does the Long-Term Chart Suggest?

Monero (XMR)

Looking beyond daily price fluctuations, the weekly and monthly charts will be particularly important in determining which cryptocurrency has the strongest potential heading into 2027.

For Monero, the key technical consideration is whether it can establish a sustained higher-high structure following its previous major market cycle. A successful retest of former resistance zones as support could lay the groundwork for another substantial move, particularly if capital rotates toward privacy-focused assets.

XMR also benefits from a relatively predictable supply model. Its permanent tail emission produces 0.6 XMR every two minutes, with an inflation rate that gradually declines over time.

Zcash, meanwhile, has a more conventional fixed supply of 21 million coins, giving it a familiar scarcity narrative. Its longer-term technical outlook will depend heavily on whether it can maintain gains tied to its growing institutional profile and establish stronger historical support.

Both could benefit enormously from a broader cryptocurrency bull market, although ZEC’s previous outperformance means investors should also consider the possibility of profit-taking and deeper corrections.

Which Privacy Coin Could Deliver the Biggest Gains in 2027?

There are compelling arguments for both projects, but their potential price trajectories could look quite different. In an optimistic 2027 scenario, Zcash could target a broad trading range of $1,600–$2,400, supported by institutional demand, increased shielded transaction adoption, and a stronger position within the privacy sector.

Monero could potentially push towards $900–$1,400, with a particularly bullish scenario opening the door to even higher valuations if demand for censorship-resistant digital cash accelerates.

These are speculative price scenarios, not technical guarantees, and regulatory restrictions remain a substantial risk for both projects. Nevertheless, one important consideration could give XMR the advantage: its established position as a dedicated privacy currency.

Zcash arguably has the stronger institutional narrative, but Monero arguably has the stronger proposition for users who consider financial privacy non-negotiable. If that distinction becomes increasingly important during the next market cycle, demand for XMR could accelerate considerably.

Gemini AI Predicts the Top Privacy Coin for 2027: Monero (XMR)

While Zcash could continue attracting institutional capital and potentially deliver impressive returns, I believe Monero has the ingredients for a stronger percentage gain over the longer term.

Its established reputation, mandatory privacy architecture, and potential to benefit from renewed demand for financial anonymity make it an intriguing candidate. If privacy becomes one of crypto’s defining investment narratives in 2027, XMR could be one of the biggest beneficiaries.

title: Bitcoin Is a Better Bet Than COIN Despite Anthropic Narrative, Analyst Says
description:
Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) still beats Coinbase (NASDAQ:COIN) stock as an investment, according to Milk Road’s in-house analyst Martin.
Analyst Sees Attractive Risk-Reward In Bitcoin
Bitcoin traded near $63,000 Wednesday, down roughly 50% from its all-time high, after closing six straight weekly candles in the red, something that has happened only a handful of times since 2013. 
Martin sees the setup still favoring buyers, since the downside looks limited even if Bitcoin dips into the $50,000s while the long-term upside stays far bigger.
That’s why he’s dollar-cost averaging into Bitcoin every month instead of trying to time the bottom, calling the current zone near $63,000 an attractive entry for anyone with a three-to-five-year horizon.
Why Martin Is Passing On Anthropic’s IPO
Anthropic’s IPO, which priced the company near $1.2 trillion to $1.3 trillion, looks fairly valued rather than cheap, Martin explained, so he isn’t buying, especially with the company’s heavy compute costs and a Wall Street base case that assumes a steep $400 billion to $500 billion run rate by 2030.
He also pointed to a broader liquidity squeeze weighing on crypto, with U.S. bonds yielding around 5% risk-free and capital flowing into megadeal IPOs like Anthropic and SpaceX instead.
Robinhood Pulls Ahead Of Coinbase
Coinbase is down 52% this year and trading around $112. "Robinhood has won the retail side of things," Martin noted, pointing to Robinhood (NASDAQ:HOOD) as the go-to venue for active traders while Coinbase leans harder into stablecoin infrastructure and custody.
Martin sold his Coinbase position months ago and is waiting on a cheaper valuation before buying back in, saying he still isn’t sure "what’s the next catalyst for them to really move the needle" on growth.
Competition is building elsewhere too, with Revolut recently raising funding at a $125 billion valuation, which Martin called ‘three or four times bigger than Coinbase,’ and now expanding into the U.S. in a move that threatens both Coinbase and Robinhood’s retail turf.
Martin also flagged billionaire investor Stanley Druckenmiller’s comment that he’s sitting mostly in cash because he can’t recall "a time with less visibility" into where markets head next, a signal Martin said is pushing him to hold more cash of his own right now.

title: Strategy (MSTR) Shares Tumble for Sixth Straight Day to $86 as Bitcoin Slides
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Strategy (MSTR) Shares Tumble for Sixth Straight Day to $86 as Bitcoin Slides
Strategy shares fell 4.6% to $86.13 on Thursday, their sixth straight decline, as bitcoin dipped below $62,000. The company's 850,849 BTC are now worth about $11 billion less than it paid.
This post Strategy (MSTR) Shares Tumble for Sixth Straight Day to $86 as Bitcoin Slides first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Strategy (MSTR) Shares Tumble for Sixth Straight Day to $86 as Bitcoin Slides

Strategy (MSTR) shares fell 4.6% on Thursday to close at $86.13, their sixth straight daily decline, as bitcoin dipped below $62,000 and a broad selloff hit U.S. stocks. In after hours trading, shares were down to $85.50.

The stock opened near $93 and slid through the afternoon, finishing near its low of about $86. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped more than 1,000 points, and the Nasdaq Composite lost about 2.1%. Bitcoin touched a low of $61,658 during the session, its weakest price since July. It was back near $62,000 late in the afternoon.

Strategy stock extends its slide

The drop adds to a brutal month for the largest corporate holder of bitcoin. Strategy shares are down about 37% from their $136.02 close on Oct. 19, and down about 29% from the $121.07 close on Nov. 10, which is when the latest leg lower began. Thursday was the stock’s sixth consecutive losing session.

The slide has wiped out most of the year’s value. Strategy closed 2025 at $151.95, which puts the stock down about 43% in 2026. The shares fell below $100 on Tuesday and now trade about 11% below Tuesday’s $96.50 close. That day they also dipped under the company’s STRC preferred for the first time since mid-August.

Thursday’s move tracked bitcoin closely. Institutions have kept buying even so, and a New York state pension fund boosted its stake by more than 10% in a recent filing. The bitcoin price slumped under $62,000 as traders weighed the risk of Federal Reserve rate hikes and a sharp pullback in technology stocks.

Holdings now sit well below cost

Strategy added 485 bitcoin in the week ending Nov. 15, according to its Nov. 16 Form 8-K. It paid $33.4 million, or an average of $68,887 per coin, and its total reached 850,849 BTC.

Those coins cost $64.20 billion, or an average of $75,452 each. With bitcoin near $62,000, the stack is worth roughly $52.8 billion, which leaves Strategy with an unrealized loss of about $11 billion. Bitcoin is trading about 18% below the company’s average purchase price.

The 850,849 coins are more than 4% of bitcoin’s 21 million supply cap, and the company also held about $4.9 billion in U.S. dollar reserves as of Nov. 15, which gives it a cushion for preferred dividends and buybacks. Strategy has not announced a new purchase since that filing. It has reported its buys on Mondays in recent weeks, so the next update would normally come Monday.

Preferred buybacks take priority

Most of Strategy’s recent cash has gone to its preferred stock instead of bitcoin. In the same filing, the company said it repurchased 2,282,510 shares of its STRC preferred for $228.1 million, nearly seven times what it spent on bitcoin.

It funded the purchases with $244.7 million raised from selling common stock. The 8-K shows $332.2 million remaining under the preferred repurchase program and $1.0 billion under its common stock buyback authorization.

Executive Chairman Michael Saylor said on X that Strategy plans to keep going. He wrote that STRC traded more than $600 million on Wednesday, calling it the only one of 456 U.S.-listed income preferreds to do so this year.

He said the buybacks add liquidity, lower dividend obligations and strengthen the credit. “We intend to keep buying below $100,” Saylor wrote.

This post Strategy (MSTR) Shares Tumble for Sixth Straight Day to $86 as Bitcoin Slides first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

Executive Chairman Michael Saylor said on X that Strategy plans to keep going. He wrote that STRC traded more than $600 million on Wednesday, calling it the only one of 456 U.S.-listed income preferreds to do so this year.

He said the buybacks add liquidity, lower dividend obligations and strengthen the credit. “We intend to keep buying below $100,” Saylor wrote.

This post Strategy (MSTR) Shares Tumble for Sixth Straight Day to $86 as Bitcoin Slides first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
