Authors: @santidipaolo, @jpinasco, @agustinpolfinance (POL Finance)

On Uniswap, the first trade of a block is often an arbitrageur hitting a price up to 12 seconds old, and liquidity providers pay for it. PropAMMs on Ethereum avoid this by having the market maker stream prices to block builders, at the cost of trusting those builders to keep their word on ordering. This post follows one trade through that system, second by second.

Highlights

  • AMM vs propAMM. On a classic AMM the price only moves when someone trades, so arbitrageurs pick off stale prices and liquidity providers pay. On a propAMM one market maker streams new prices to the builders, the companies that assemble Ethereum blocks, and they write the latest price into the block right before your trade.
  • Your trade fills at a current price. What you see when you sign is an estimate. The price you get is the maker’s latest update, written into the block. In one swap we traced, that update was signed 0.8 s after the block’s slot started. A late update still gets in because builders keep bidding for a block for a second or more into its slot. The trade had been built almost 10 s earlier; that includes the user’s time to sign, so the mechanism itself is faster. Through the LambdaClass router, a trade goes to the best offer standing when the block is built. A direct trade is protected only by its minimum-output limit.
  • The maker finds out late. The maker learns it was filled only when it sees the block, a median 1.23 s after it signed its price, against milliseconds on a centralized exchange. Until then it cannot hedge. That gap is what the spread pays for: the shorter it gets, the tighter the maker can quote.

What a propAMM is

A propAMM (proprietary AMM) is an on-chain pool whose liquidity and price belong to a single market maker. The maker rewrites the price whenever it wants, hundreds of times per Ethereum block (LambdaClass). To the trader, the taker, it looks like any AMM: call a contract, get tokens. To the maker it works like an order book: it quotes a bid and an ask around its own fair value, instead of along a reserve curve.

PropAMMs went live on Ethereum mainnet in May 2026. In the week of 14–20 September 2026 the two largest, Fermi and Metric, traded 280M and 178M USD: together 7.6% of Uniswap’s 6.0B USD that week. ethresear.ch puts propAMMs at 5–10% of mainnet swap volume, and at ~40% of volume across the largest venues on Solana, where the model started (ethresear.ch).


Figure 1. ethresear.ch 26129, week of 14–20 Sep 2026

Two designs it is easy to confuse it with:

  • A curve AMM (Uniswap) prices from the pool’s reserves, so the price changes only when someone trades. A propAMM’s price changes when the maker decides, using the maker’s own closed-source model.
  • An RFQ (Hashflow, 0x RFQ) has the taker request a signed quote by API and carry it inside its own transaction. On a propAMM the price sits in the contract, and the taker executes against whatever it says when the transaction runs.

On Ethereum the line between the two is blurrier than on Solana, and that is what this post is about.

Why it started on Solana, and what breaks on Ethereum

A propAMM works only if the maker’s price update runs before an arbitrageur can trade against the old price.

On Solana the chain gives that for free. Blocks come every ~400 ms (a slot). A price update costs ~500–700 compute units (CU, Solana’s measure of execution cost) against ≥17,000 for a swap (arXiv 2609.38056), and the leader orders transactions by fee per CU. The maker pays little, lands first, and can update many times per second.


Figure 2. arXiv 2609.38056

On Ethereum that breaks for three reasons (ethresear.ch 25543):

  1. Slots are 12 s. By the end of a slot, any price set at its start is stale.
  2. Every update pays the network’s base fee, whether anyone trades or not.
  3. Block builders choose the order. Ethereum blocks are assembled by specialised companies, the builders, that bid for the right to build each block through MEV-Boost; the validator who proposes the block (the proposer) takes the highest bid. A builder could drop the maker’s update and sell the arbitrage against the old price.

The fix moved the guarantee to the builders. Titan published a propAMM API, later adopted by Quasar, BuilderNet and Bombora (ethresear.ch). The maker streams signed updates to them instead of sending transactions (Titan docs). Each builder keeps only the latest update per pool, writes it into the block immediately before the first trade against that pool, and skips it if nobody trades. That ordering is a promise by four companies, enforced by nothing in the protocol. Proposals to standardise it exist, such as ERC-8324, but none is live.

Layer 2s are a different case. Base produces 200 ms sub-blocks (Flashblocks) ordered by fee (Base docs), so the Solana approach roughly works there. This post is about Ethereum L1.

One trade, step by step

Five parties take part: the maker, the taker, an aggregator that finds the taker a price, the builder, and the proposer. The price the taker gets is the last update the maker sent the builder before the trade; what was on-chain when the taker signed plays no part.


Figure 3. One Ethereum slot · illustrative timing; rule from ethresear.ch 26129 and Titan docs

  1. Before anyone trades. The maker reads exchange prices, runs its pricing model, signs a price update and streams it to Titan, Quasar, BuilderNet and Bombora, hundreds of times per block, one every few tens of milliseconds (PropAMM Factory). None of it touches the chain yet.
  2. Quote. The taker’s wallet or aggregator asks for a price. The pool’s on-chain price is stale, so the aggregator simulates the trade against a preview the builder publishes: the pool as it would look with the latest update (LambdaClass).
  3. Sign and send. The taker signs an ordinary transaction with a minimum output, minOut: if the trade would return less, it reverts. The transaction goes privately to the builders and skips the public mempool, where everyone could see it (Bombora docs).
  4. Wait for a block. A new block comes every 12 s, so a trade that makes the next one waits up to 12 s, ~6 s on average. One that misses it waits for the following block. Meanwhile the maker keeps repricing, and the builder matches the trade only against an update at least 50 ms newer than the trade itself.
  5. Block building. The builder writes the maker’s latest update immediately before the first trade against that pool; later trades in the same block use the same update. A trade sent through the LambdaClass PropAMM Router is requoted at this point against every propAMM, goes to the best offer, and falls back to Uniswap v3 if none beats minOut.
  6. Inclusion. The block is proposed at the start of the next slot and reaches most of the network 1.5–2 s later. Titan built 44% of blocks in the period that A. Fuller’s memo covers, and carried 69% of propAMM trades (data memo).
  7. Settlement. Tokens move inside the swap itself. The block becomes final two epochs later: 2 × 32 slots × 12 s, ~12.8 minutes.

Here is one real trade against El Zorro, the propAMM run by Zonda Markets.


Figure 4. Swap 0x395370f11681ae554d7308bd93be60ad8530a638727e617e75ac5b73fea04ed7 · El Zorro on-chain data

The fill is at a current price. The swap was built at 07:50:14 UTC; we read that from the transaction’s own deadline (method in the appendix). Its block’s slot started 9 s later, and the update it executed against was signed 0.8 s after that. The user signs after the transaction is built, and the chain does not record when, so part of those 9 s is the user reading the wallet pop-up and the mechanism itself took less than 9 s. What the user saw at signing was an estimate; the price came from an update signed at execution.

What stops the maker from showing one price and filling at a worse one depends on the route. Through the LambdaClass router, the trade goes to the best offer standing when the block is built. A direct trade to one propAMM is protected only by its minOut, which caps the loss at the trader’s slippage tolerance but does not guarantee the best price inside it.

Figure 5 shows the same three timestamps for every swap against El Zorro in one day, labelled by the wallet or app that created the trade. Orders that settle through CoW wait for its batch auction, and take longer. Each line starts when the transaction was built, before the user signed, so it overstates how long the mechanism itself takes.


Figure 5. El Zorro on-chain data, 14–15 Oct 2026; origins from on-chain markers (integrator strings, CoW appData, smart-account factories)

When the maker finds out, and why that sets the spread

The block is proposed at the start of the next slot, but nobody sees it at that moment. The proposer keeps collecting builder bids for up to ~1 s, sometimes longer, and the median node receives the block 1.5–2.1 s into the slot (ethPandaOps, 50,318 blocks). No builder sends the maker a fill notification, so the maker learns of its trade only when the block reaches its own node.


Figure 6. beaconcha.in (winning-bid categories, 950 ms timeout), ethPandaOps (50,318 blocks, 25 Apr–2 May 2026), Bombora docs; maker lane: El Zorro medians

El Zorro measured this over 24 hours of mainnet (14–15 October 2026, 404 WETH trades). Its quote was signed a median 0.76 s into the slot, and its node saw the block 1.23 s after the signature; for the slowest 10% of trades it took 2.18 s or more. For those ~1.2 s the maker holds a position it does not know about and cannot hedge it on an exchange. The taker is in the same spot on the other side: it cannot act on its new tokens until the block is visible.

That window is what the spread pays for. The maker quotes wide enough to cover how far the market can move before it hedges. Price moves grow roughly with the square root of elapsed time, so a shorter window lets the maker quote tighter for the same risk. In El Zorro’s data, Binance moved by more than its half-spread (0.90 bps; one basis point, bps, is 0.01%) during the window in 16% of trades; a 2 bps half-spread would have covered all but ~5%. Every part of the window that goes away is spread that can go back to traders: a later signature, faster block propagation, or a fill signal from the builder the moment the proposer picks its block. The relay that passes the block to the proposer knows the winner before the network does, but no builder offers that signal today.

Whether the trade lands is less of a question. Trades go privately to Titan, Quasar, BuilderNet and Bombora, so a trade usually lands in the next block. The residual risk is a slot won by a builder without the API; Titan alone built 44% of blocks in the memo’s period, and we have not measured the four together.

Why the stale-price problem goes away

Compare the same trade on Uniswap. The wallet simulates the swap against the pool’s current reserves, the user signs with a slippage limit, and the swap runs against whatever the pool holds when the block is built. If the output falls below the limit the swap reverts, and the user still pays gas.

The price at the top of each block is whatever the last trade left. When ETH moves on Binance, the pool stays at the old price until an arbitrageur trades it back, and that arbitrageur pays the builder to go first. The liquidity providers’ loss to these trades is called LVR, loss-versus-rebalancing (Milionis et al. 2022). Two more costs come with the design: a swap sent to the public mempool can be sandwiched, with a searcher buying just before and selling just after inside the user’s slippage limit, and the fee is fixed per pool tier (1, 5, 30 or 100 bps on v3) whoever is trading.


Figure 7. Illustrative path, no data; LVR as in Milionis et al. (2022)

On a propAMM the builder matches a trade only against an update at least 50 ms newer than the trade (ethresear.ch; Titan calls it freshness protection and lets the threshold be configured). The taker gets a price computed after it sent its transaction, and the maker is never stuck with the previous block’s price. The 12-second-old price that arbitrageurs pick off on Uniswap does not exist; what remains is the ~1 s window from the previous section. LambdaClass puts the consequence directly: “Because makers no longer carry the risk of stale prices, they can tighten spreads and improve their quotes” (LambdaClass).

A fresh price cuts both ways: if the market moves against the taker in the meantime, the taker gets the worse price, as with a market order on an exchange. It is still not a “last look”, where the maker sees an order and decides whether to fill it. The maker never sees the trade; the builder does the pairing.

The same trade on a centralized exchange

On a centralized exchange (CEX) the trade is an internal event. The taker sends a market order; the exchange checks the balance it already holds in custody, matches the order against its book in microseconds to ~1 ms, and confirms in milliseconds. Settlement is a database entry; nothing moves on-chain until the user withdraws, hours or days later. The maker’s orders sit in the book at a known place in the queue, so the race is to get there first and cancel fast. The trade is final the moment the matching engine writes it, and the risk is the exchange itself.

The clock, side by side

On time to fill, an Ethereum propAMM is about four orders of magnitude (~10,000×) slower than a CEX (12 s against ~1 ms) and 30× slower than Solana. On the age of the price it executes against, the gap is much smaller: in El Zorro’s data the update was signed ~0.6 s before the builder sealed the block (median).


Figure 8. ethresear.ch 26129 (Solana, Ethereum slots), Base docs (Flashblocks), Ethereum finality = 2 epochs × 32 slots × 12 s; CEX range is a third-party estimate

There are two clocks. The slot clock, 12 s, sets when the trade settles. The quote clock sets how old the price is: ~0.6 s when the block is sealed, ~1.2 s when the maker sees it. On Uniswap the two are the same clock, so a slow block means a stale price; a propAMM separates them, and that is what lets it work at Ethereum’s block time. The quote clock is also the one the spread pays for.

CEX Uniswap propAMM (Ethereum)
Where the price lives The exchange’s order book Pool reserves (curve) Contract, rewritten by the maker
Who sets the order of trades Matching engine, price-time Builder, for its own profit Builder, update before trade
Age of the price at fill Microseconds Up to 12 s Signed after the trade arrives
Time to fill Microseconds to ms Next block (12 s) or later Next block (12 s) or later
Maker learns of the fill Milliseconds Not applicable (passive pool) ~1.2 s after its quote (median)
What you trust The exchange Nothing on ordering Builders to honour the rule

In numbers

Sources here are a single-author memo or interested parties.

Metric Value Source
ETH/USDC full spread (ask − bid) around the maker’s own mid, smallest size, single snapshot 1 Sep 2026 0.86 bps (Metric) to 4.20 bps (bopAMM); Fermi 2.34 bps A. Fuller memo
Capital turnover per day Fermi ~23× its 5.4M USD of liquidity; Uniswap v3 on the same pairs 0.6× its 319M USD. Memo’s own period: with the September volume above, Fermi’s would be ~7× A. Fuller memo
Gas, price update vs swap (measured on Base) ~27–33K vs 200–400K arXiv
LambdaClass Router flow ~13M USD across ~1,000 swaps per day (22 Sep 2026) LambdaClass

The turnover row is the business model: the maker does not park liquidity in the pool, it refills from its exchange inventory, so a few million dollars of capital carry volume of the same order as Uniswap’s pools on those pairs.

The trade-off

The underlying difference is who controls the order between the maker’s price and the trade: the matching engine on a CEX, nobody on Uniswap, the builder on an Ethereum propAMM. The propAMM gives the maker back its ability to react, and shrinks its exposure from a 12-second-old price to the ~1 second until it sees the block. The cost is an intermediary back in the ordering: four private builders that promise to write the update first, with nothing in the protocol enforcing it.

Appendix: for builders and market makers

A1. The slot boundary, step by step

  1. End of slot N: last updates and takes. Each maker update is valid for a single block, the next one (Bombora docs). A take is eligible only against a quote received more than the freshness buffer after it: taker_received_at + freshness_buffer < quote_received_at, using only the builder’s own receive timestamps.
  2. t = 0: getHeader. The proposer of slot N+1 asks the relays for the best header. The MEV-Boost default timeout is 950 ms, under a hard limit of ~1 s (beaconcha.in). Until the winning bid is committed, builders keep re-bidding, and Titan re-evaluates candidates on every quote update (Titan docs).
  3. 0 to 3.5 s: winning bid committed. beaconcha.in classifies the time from slot start to the committed winning bid as on-time (≤ 1,200 ms), timing games (1,201–2,600 ms) or aggressive (> 2,600 ms). Proposers who wait collect higher bids.
  4. Sign, getPayload, broadcast. The proposer signs the blinded header, calls getPayload, and the relay publishes the block. No per-step latency is published. The relay knows which bid won at getPayload, before anyone else sees the block.
  5. ~1.5–2.1 s: the network sees the block. The median node sees it 104 ms (9 KB block) to 348 ms (238 KB) after first sighting, p99 427–1,248 ms; from slot start, the median is 1,505–2,122 ms (ethPandaOps).
  6. t = 4 s: attestation deadline. Attesters vote with or without the block. Proposing at ~3–3.5 s already costs ~10% wrong-head votes (ethresear.ch 20272, Jul–Aug 2024).
  7. The maker learns of the fill. Neither Titan nor Bombora documents a fill notification; Bombora’s ACK only confirms the update was forwarded, and stale or reverting quotes are dropped silently. PropAMM Factory runs per-block landing checks (LambdaClass). In El Zorro’s 24 h sample its node saw the block a median 1.99 s into slot N+1 (p10 1.62 s, p90 3.41 s) and its pusher ~160 ms later. Blocks arrive in two regimes, around 1.7–1.8 s and 3.2–3.4 s; when the block is sealed late the builder takes a later signature, so the quote’s age stays the same.
  8. Rebalance. The maker hedges on a CEX in milliseconds or tops up on-chain inventory. No public source measures maker hedging latency. On Base, Tessera refills from opposite on-chain flow without hedging (arXiv).

A2. How fresh in practice

El Zorro, 24 h of mainnet, 14–15 Oct 2026, 404 WETH inclusions. The included quote was signed a median 0.76 s after the slot started. The builder sealed ~0.61 s after the signature (an upper bound, from Titan’s public stream). El Zorro’s node saw the block 1.23 s after the signature (p10 0.84 s, p90 2.18 s). Titan, BuilderNet and Quasar give the same distribution, and nothing is included younger than 0.5 s.

Over that window ETHUSDT on Binance moved a median 0.04 bps and 1.72 bps at p90, against a published half-spread of 0.90 bps (median). The move exceeded the half-spread in 16% of inclusions; a 2 bps half-spread would cut that to ~5%. Stablecoin pairs are a separate population: the quote is re-signed only when the price moves, so a median age of 6.9 s costs nothing.

A3. How a maker implements it: El Zorro

El Zorro runs on PropAMM Factory, LambdaClass’s open-source kit:

  • a quote updater reads exchange feeds, runs a pricing model per pair, signs updates and streams them to builders, repricing “throughout the block”;
  • pricing models range from a fixed price to exchange prices with spreads that widen with volatility and inventory;
  • the propAMM contract reads the price from a Priority Update Registry and fills the trade;
  • operations: landing checks, circuit breakers, alerts, and a Postgres record of every published quote.

A4. How we time a transaction

The chain does not record when a transaction was built or signed. Wallets and aggregators set a swap’s deadline to the moment they build it plus a round time-to-live (TTL): 600, 1,200, 1,800 or 3,600 s. Taking the round value just above deadline − block time recovers the TTL, and deadline − TTL gives when the transaction was built. Bot flow drops out, because bots do not set the deadline that way. That leaves 39 WETH swaps: 24 direct and 15 CoW orders, whose time also includes CoW’s batch auction. The deadline is set before the wallet asks the user to sign, so any time measured from it includes the user’s signing time and is an upper bound on the mechanism’s own latency.

A5. Full comparison

CEX AMM (Uniswap v3/v4) propAMM (Ethereum L1) RFQ (Hashflow, 0x RFQ)
Where the price lives Matching engine’s book Pool reserves (curve) Contract state, rewritten by the maker Off-chain signed quote
Who moves it Maker, at will Only trades Maker, streamed to the builder Maker, on request
Who orders Matching engine, price-time Builder, for its own profit Builder, update-before-take rule Taker carries the quote in its tx
Age of the price at fill µs Up to 12 s (last trade) ≥ 50 ms newer than the take Up to quote expiry
Time to fill ~1 ms Next slot (12 s) or later Next slot (12 s) or later Next slot (12 s) or later

Maker’s adverse selection Cancel race LVR to the arbitrageur Window between update and take Quote validity window

title: Ledger Faces Growing Scrutiny as Dubai Users Report Mysterious Crypto Losses
description: One Dubai user claims to have lost 507K USDT from their Ledger Flex, while another is said to have lost 122K USDT also from a Ledger device.
fullContent:
Hardware wallet manufacturer Ledger has verified reports of tampered devices showing up in Berlin and is also investigating two suspected cases in Dubai.

According to the company, the newly identified wallets carry the same physical modification as those seen in October in Southeast Asia.

Ledger Investigates Dubai Reports

On November 15, a trader, Rewinsky, posted on X that they had lost $1,300 SOL from their Ledger and, after checking the device, shared pictures on the social platform allegedly showing it had been tampered with.

Days later, another account, New Babylon Order, made similar claims that someone had drained 507,000 USDT from a Ledger Stax they had bought at the Virgin Megastore in Dubai in early October. According to them, they generated the wallet’s seed directly on the device and did not type it anywhere else. There was reportedly a second victim who had bought their Ledger wallet in the same Dubai store; this one said to have lost 122,000 USDT.

Yesterday, Ledger published an update, where it said that it was reviewing the Dubai cases and that its investigations had identified devices in Berlin that had been tampered with. Recall that in October, a user who had purchased their device through MediaMarkt in Germany claimed it showed possible signs of manipulation.

The French firm also confirmed that it had found one affected Ledger Nano Gen5 in Southeast Asia.

“Every device we have confirmed shows the same kind of physical modification, built to capture the recovery phrase during setup,” wrote the wallet maker in the report.

When the issue first came to light in October, Ledger said that an organized criminal gang was behind it, buying genuine devices over several months and then fitting them with custom-built components that could capture recovery phrases when the wallets were being set up. The group is then believed to have put the hardware wallets back into circulation through resellers like CryptoBilis in Southeast Asia.

Security analyst Mark Karpelès also speculated that the implants were professionally manufactured, complete with production lines and manuals, and then sold to intermediaries, who installed them on Ledger devices before reselling them.

Ledger has not ruled out the possibility that more affected wallets will be discovered. It also asked any users who had concerns about their devices being tampered with to reach out to support and said that it was working with partners and law enforcement authorities to find such devices as quickly as possible.

Possible Losses in the Millions

As CryptoPotato reported, devices sold through CryptoBilis in Indonesia, the Philippines, and Malaysia may have caused as much as $80 million worth of losses, with blockchain analytics firm Bitquery saying the figure could be as high as $102 million from 335 wallets on 5 blockchains.

Ledger has urged anyone who may have bought any of its devices from third parties in Germany or Southeast Asia not to use them to set up or restore a wallet. It also advised such users to move their funds to new wallets and only create recovery phrases from devices bought directly from its official website.

title: Swiss Bank Sygnum Says Bitcoin Could Reach New High Near $128,000
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

Swiss Bank Sygnum Says Bitcoin Could Reach New High Near $128,000
The Swiss bank estimates bitcoin could hit a new all-time high near $128,000 and calls the current downturn the shallowest bear market to date, as bitcoin moves into reserve portfolios.
This post Swiss Bank Sygnum Says Bitcoin Could Reach New High Near $128,000 first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

Swiss Bank Sygnum Says Bitcoin Could Reach New High Near $128,000

Sygnum Bank estimates that bitcoin could reach a new all-time high near $128,000. The Swiss digital asset bank laid out the scenario in its 2027 Sygnal outlook on Thursday, alongside a call that bitcoin and ether will both set new highs while the broader market stays narrow.

The report also frames the current downturn as the shallowest bear market for bitcoin to date. Sygnum puts the drawdown at around 54%, compared with declines of more than 70% in previous cycles, and says digital assets enter 2027 with lower structural volatility and stronger fundamentals.

The outlook arrives as bitcoin trades near $63,000 after six straight weekly losses and a drop below its 200-week moving average. Sygnum’s case is that the market has changed since earlier cycles, not that the slide is over.

Sygnum describes a more mature market. Volatility is increasingly driven by broader dollar liquidity and market structure, it said, and institutions have added new channels through ETFs, leveraged trading and crypto-backed credit. By the end of October, stablecoin supply stood near $298 billion and tokenized real-world assets exceeded $39 billion.

How bitcoin gets to $128,000

The estimate rests on a rotation out of technology stocks. Digital assets are worth about 6% of the Nasdaq’s market value, and Sygnum calculates that if 0.75% of Nasdaq value, roughly $360 billion, moved into crypto, total market capitalization could rise by more than 60%.

In that scenario, bitcoin would reach a new high near $128,000. The report does not put a date on it and describes the figure as an estimate built on Sygnum’s own calculations, not a price target. It also notes that a sell-off in AI stocks could spill into crypto. Currently, Anthropic’s record $81 billion IPO is set to open about 25% to 30% above its $83 offering price, which has lifted AI and chip stocks, but worries about higher interest rates have pulled the Nasdaq back from an early 2% gain to about 0.3%.

Bitcoin moves into the reserve bucket

Behind the price call is a shift in how institutions treat bitcoin. Sygnum predicts it will move out of the tactical sleeve of portfolios and into the “strategic reserve bucket,” competing with gold for capital that wants protection against currency debasement. BlackRock, Morgan Stanley and Bank of America each recommend allocations of 1% to 4%.

The report says 2027 should reward selection over broad market exposure. Sygnum expects adoption to concentrate in stablecoins, tokenized assets, bitcoin as an institutional macro asset and tokens with proven usage, and it believes investors will be rewarded for choosing assets with real usage and revenue.

The math is simple, according to the report. Bitcoin is worth about 6% of gold’s market value, so moving just 1% of gold’s value into it would lift its market capitalization by at least 17%.

Large holders have already shown that appetite. BlackRock has said security concerns are pushing bitcoin whales into its spot ETF, even as miners such as MARA have sold coins to raise cash.

The rest of the 2027 outlook

Sygnum also expects tokens that return revenue to holders to outperform, stablecoin settlement at Visa to triple to $60 billion by the fourth quarter of 2027, and carry trades, which pair long spot with short futures, to beat Treasury bills. That comes after the Federal Reserve’s September rate rise to 3.75%–4.00% and 67 straight days of negative bitcoin funding rates in 2026. It describes regulation as clearer but still incomplete, with Europe’s MiCA regime now fully operational and U.S. agencies still advancing rules for crypto markets.

Fabian Dori, Sygnum’s chief investment officer and lead author, said volatility “has not disappeared; it has just migrated from the asset itself to its plumbing,” and that institutional adoption “has kept on building.”

“To understand the shape of 2027 markets, investors must look past price to fundamentals,” Dori said.

This post Swiss Bank Sygnum Says Bitcoin Could Reach New High Near $128,000 first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

title: Sui Price May Slip to $0.60 Unless Hashi Wakes Bitcoin's 'Idle Capital', Fluid CEO Says
description: Sui launched Hashi on mainnet so Bitcoin holders can mint hBTC and borrow USDC on Fluid. SUI hovers above $0.64 support as sellers keep control of the trend.
fullContent:
Quick Take

  • Sui launched Hashi on mainnet, letting Bitcoin holders mint hBTC and borrow USDC on Fluid.
  • SUI still trades beneath both major moving averages, with sellers steering momentum.
  • The nearest floor near $0.64 may decide whether the slide deepens.

Sui switched on Hashi, its Bitcoin finance layer, with backing from custodians, market makers and lending apps. The pitch is simple. BTC holders can put idle coins to work on Sui without selling them.

The token has not cheered the news. SUI kept sliding through the weeks partners lined up, and pledged capital has yet to become real deposits. Traders now want to know if hBTC demand arrives before sellers push the price to fresh lows.

Hashi Brings Bitcoin Lending to Sui Mainnet

Sui launched Hashi, its native Bitcoin finance layer, on mainnet on Nov. 19, 2026, with more than 20 partners. Holders deposit BTC on the Bitcoin network and receive hBTC, a token backed 1:1. They can use hBTC in Sui lending and other apps, then burn it to get their BTC back.

Fluid is the first big use case. The protocol lets users borrow USDC against hBTC collateral. "Bitcoin is the largest pool of idle capital in crypto. With Hashi, it can now power deep, capital-efficient credit markets on Fluid," founder and CEO Samyak Jain said.

Anchorage Digital will give institutions access through its custody bank, Atlas settlement and Porto wallet, CEO Nathan McCauley said. Cumberland and Wave Digital Assets will supply BTC and stablecoin liquidity. HoneyB opened two vaults via Upshift, one in hBTC and one in USDC. Concrete, Bluefin, Cetus, Current, Suilend and Merkl also signed on. BitGo access is planned for early 2027, with Ember vaults due later in 2026.

Mysten Labs introduced Hashi in March and opened a public testnet in July. The more than $500 million in commitments disclosed Oct. 8 were pledges. None of that has yet shown up as deposits, so real adoption remains unproven.

SUI Trades Far Beneath Both Major Averages

Sui (SUI) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

SUI traded near $0.71 at last check. Buyers have not stepped in on the news.

The 50-day moving average, which tracks the average closing price over roughly the past ten weeks, sits near $0.87. The 200-day average, a gauge of the longer trend, is higher still at about $0.95. With price below both lines, each one now acts as a ceiling.

That setup marks a clear downtrend. The shorter average also sits beneath the longer one, so recent prices have been weaker than the yearly norm. Traders often read that pattern as sellers holding the upper hand.

SUI is down about 28% over the past month. It also shed roughly 13% in the last seven days alone.

The launch headlines have so far failed to reverse the slide.

The past day looked calmer. SUI slipped only about 1% in 24 hours, a much smaller move than the weekly pace. Selling seems to be slowing, but it has not stopped.

A quieter session can mean sellers are tiring, or it can be a pause before the next leg lower.

Sellers Still Steer Momentum Despite Oversold Edge

The daily RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, reads about 33. Readings below 30 count as oversold, so SUI sits just above that line. Sellers have pushed hard, but the gauge has not yet flashed the kind of exhaustion that often comes before a bounce.

The MACD, which compares short and longer price trends, remains below its signal line. That means momentum is still pointing down.

The ADX shows a real trend in place, and sellers are the ones driving it. A strong trend led by sellers tends to persist until buyers show up with size.

An oversold reading alone rarely turns a market. SUI would need RSI to dip and then curl higher, alongside a MACD crossover, before a rebound looks credible.

$0.64 Is the Floor Between SUI and $0.60

The nearest support sits near $0.64, and the daily chart shows no second floor below it.

A daily close under that level would leave the token with little to catch it. The next obvious stop would be the headline target near $0.60. Because no buyers have defended that zone recently, a slide there could come quickly.

The upside map is clearer. First resistance stands near $0.80. A move back above it would be the first sign that hBTC demand is lifting SUI.

Beyond that, the next ceiling lines up with the 200-day average already overhead. Clearing both levels would mark a real shift in the trend.

What Could Flip SUI Over the Next Three Days

Both paths for the next three days hinge on the same pair of levels.

  • Bullish: Early hBTC deposits on Fluid and the HoneyB vaults give buyers a reason to return. A daily close above $0.80 would confirm that demand and open room toward the 200-day average. A break of support would cancel this view.
  • Bearish: Pledges stay pledges and sellers keep control. A break under $0.64 would put $0.60 in play quickly. A reclaim of resistance would invalidate this case.

Hashi Needs Deposits Before the Chart Turns

The bias stays bearish. SUI needs proof that BTC holders are actually minting hBTC and borrowing on Fluid.

Committed capital may never show up as deposits. Any bridge glitch or custody problem would also hurt confidence in Hashi quickly. Watch on-chain hBTC supply for the first real signal.

fullContent:
What if Bitcoin’s next major rally isn’t just another cryptocurrency bull run, but the start of a fundamental shift in how the world’s largest economies view money? Perplexity AI predicts Bitcoin’s 2027 price target, offering an in-depth look at how it could reach such an insane level.

Sovereign adoption, rising institutional demand, monetary easing, and growing concerns over government debt could create the conditions for an extraordinary Bitcoin rally in 2027.

(SOURCE: Perplexity AI Predicts a Bullish BTC Price Target for 2027)

While a seven-figure price for Bitcoin may still seem outrageous, the key factors supporting such a valuation are becoming harder to ignore. With a fixed supply of 21 million coins, an expanding institutional infrastructure, and governments starting to consider Bitcoin as a strategic reserve asset, the long-term investment outlook is evolving.

However, reaching $1M would require an unprecedented influx of capital. Could 2027 be the year when Bitcoin takes a giant leap toward that milestone? A particularly bullish scenario might drive Bitcoin’s value much higher than many investors currently expect.

Could Governments Start Treating Bitcoin Like Digital Gold?

(SOURCE: CoinGecko)

One of the most significant potential catalysts is sovereign adoption. In March 2025, US President Donald Trump signed an executive order establishing a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve, creating an official framework for holding government-owned Bitcoin rather than automatically selling seized assets. However, the proposed reserve remains subject to administrative and legislative uncertainty.

The bigger development would be an announcement that the US intends to acquire additional Bitcoin through a government-backed purchasing program.

If other major economies followed suit, the resulting competition for a limited supply could fundamentally change BTC’s valuation.

Institutional demand is another important consideration. US spot Bitcoin ETFs added approximately 79,800 BTC during the third quarter of 2026, almost twice the amount newly mined during the same period. This demonstrates how quickly institutional investment vehicles can absorb available supply when demand returns.

Imagine that trend accelerating throughout 2027, with pension funds, sovereign wealth funds and major asset managers increasing their allocations. Bitcoin could experience a substantial supply-demand imbalance.

EXPLORE: 9+ Best High-Risk, High-Reward Crypto to Buy in 2026

Perplexity AI Predicts The Macroeconomic Perfect Storm Could Spark a Parabolic BTC Run

Bitcoin’s next major rally could also depend on developments outside the cryptocurrency industry. Government debt, persistent fiscal deficits, and concerns surrounding fiat currency purchasing power could strengthen the argument for scarce alternative assets.

A particularly bullish macroeconomic scenario would involve central banks cutting interest rates as inflation moderates, alongside renewed liquidity injections and an expanding global money supply.

Historically, Bitcoin has benefited from improving liquidity conditions, although its relationship with global money supply is not guaranteed to persist. Fidelity Digital Assets has highlighted how the relationship has become less reliable during recent market conditions.

If financial conditions become significantly more accommodative in 2027, risk appetite could return to cryptocurrency markets. Another potential catalyst is the next Bitcoin halving, expected in 2028. Although it falls outside the 2027 forecast, markets could begin pricing in its impact beforehand, particularly as investors anticipate another reduction in newly issued BTC.

Combined, these developments could create a powerful narrative around Bitcoin’s increasingly scarce supply and growing monetary significance.

What Does the Long-Term Technical Picture Suggest?

Market Cap

From a higher-timeframe perspective, Bitcoin’s ability to establish a sustained bullish structure will be essential.

Rather than focusing on daily fluctuations, investors should watch the monthly chart for higher highs and higher lows, along with improving momentum indicators and sustained trading volume.

A decisive move above previous cycle resistance zones, followed by successful retests, could signal the beginning of another major expansion phase.

The $200,000–$300,000 region would represent an important psychological milestone in a bullish scenario, while sustained institutional accumulation could potentially support a move beyond those levels. However, a seven-figure valuation would require much more than a conventional bull market.

Could Bitcoin Reach $500,000 in 2027?

For Bitcoin to reach $1M, its market capitalization would approach $20 trillion, based on a circulating supply of roughly 20 million coins. That would put it in direct competition with gold as a global store of value.

While not impossible over a longer timeframe, achieving that valuation in 2027 would require an extraordinary convergence of events.

My bullish Bitcoin prediction for 2027 is $500,000, with a potential trading range of $350,000–$500,000 under an exceptionally favorable combination of institutional adoption, sovereign accumulation, and improving global liquidity.

I believe $1M remains a longer-term possibility, but $500,000 is an ambitious yet more defensible target for the next major market expansion.

If governments begin competing for Bitcoin, institutional demand accelerates, and central banks turn towards easier monetary policy, the road to seven figures could become considerably shorter than many expect.

The post XRP Has an Institutional Edge, But Garlinghouse Believes Wall Street Is Pulling Liquidity Away appeared first on Cryptonews.
fullContent:
The XRP price is struggling to take advantage of institutional credibility for the ledger. Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse has another explanation: Wall Street is pulling liquidity toward blockbuster IPOs.

The XRP Ledger Foundation assessed the network against all ten principles in the Global Layer One (GL1) Market Infrastructure Toolkit. CertiK independently verified the network’s evidence under the Architecture and Resiliency principles.

Garlinghouse said investors have been moving money out of crypto, including XRP, to fund major listings. He expects the market to recover after Anthropic’s debut, just as it did following SpaceX’s IPO.

XRPL Adds an Institutional Credential

The GL1 toolkit gives financial institutions a common framework for assessing digital infrastructure. It has ten principles that cover governance, legal foundations, settlement finality, architecture, economic models, resilience, access, interoperability, privacy, and operations.

This makes the assessment relevant to banks exploring tokenized markets. Institutions need to understand how networks handle operational risk, governance, and settlement before building financial products on them.

XRPL’s case is notable because it is public and permissionless. Traditional financial networks often operate behind controlled access. Public blockchains must show how risks are handled across distributed governance, protocol upgrades, and open participation.

The Foundation assessed XRPL against all ten principles. It also supplied supporting evidence for each control. CertiK then examined the Architecture and Resiliency sections, using code, configurations, logs, and test results.

CertiK said it reviewed all 112 controls in the toolkit. Its technical verification focused on those suitable for independent assessment. The firm also verified Partior’s self-attestation under the same two principles.

The XRPL Foundation called it the first such verification for a public, permissionless Layer 1. The milestone gives institutions a structured reference when evaluating networks for tokenized deposits, stablecoins, funds, and other assets.

That is useful progress for XRPL’s institutional pitch. Risk and compliance teams can now examine evidence against familiar market-infrastructure standards. They have more than a blockchain’s own description of its capabilities.

Garlinghouse Looks to Anthropic IPO for XRP Price Relief

Xrp (XRP)
24h7d30d1yAll time

In today’s interview, Garlinghouse addressed the gap between Ripple’s expansion and XRP price performance. He said the SpaceX IPO triggered a similar pullback as investors shifted liquidity out of crypto. He specifically named Bitcoin and XRP among the assets affected.

Investors moved capital from liquid crypto markets into the highly anticipated SpaceX listing, he said. Garlinghouse sees the same pattern ahead of Anthropic’s debut.

Anthropic priced its shares at $83 and began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on Thursday. The offering covers 980 million shares, and the deal is expected to close Friday, November 20.

“What we saw after the SpaceX IPO was a rally in the crypto markets,” Garlinghouse said. “I think you’ll see that happen here as well.”

He also expects digital assets to stop moving in lockstep. In his view, real utility and demand will increasingly separate stronger projects from speculative tokens. That puts the XRP price debate back on XRPL’s ability to attract activity.

Bitcoin Hyper Races Toward Presale Deadline With $33M Raised

Bitcoin Hyper is chasing a similar infrastructure opportunity as XRPL, this time around Bitcoin. Its Layer 2 combines Solana Virtual Machine (SVM) technology with Bitcoin settlement, aiming to bring faster transactions, DeFi applications, and staking to the Bitcoin ecosystem.

The project has already rolled out its public testnet, explorer, wallet, faucet, bridge, and staking portal. These releases give developers and early users a working environment to explore before the planned mainnet rollout.

The presale has raised more than $33.2 million, with HYPER priced at just $0.0136. The November 26 deadline is now approaching, leaving just seven days before the scheduled presale close.

XRPL’s latest institutional milestone shows how infrastructure improvements can strengthen a blockchain’s appeal to financial players. Bitcoin Hyper is pursuing a different route, building an execution layer that could make Bitcoin more useful across payments and decentralized finance.

If Bitcoin Layer 2 adoption gains traction, projects delivering faster execution and financial applications could attract growing institutional attention. Bitcoin Hyper is positioning itself ahead of that opportunity, with its presale entering its final stretch.

The post Creature In Basement Helping With The Rat Problem appeared first on The Onion.
fullContent:
LEWISTON, ME—Admitting that the wet sounds of it crawling around at night were far preferable to the racket of squeaking and scratching in the walls, local man Scott Burgess told reporters Thursday the creature in his basement was really helping with the rat problem. “When I saw that thing’s tail whip around a dark corner of the cellar, I thought it might be a problem, but it seems to have scared off a lot of the rats,” said Burgess, who added that people often only think about the evil aspects of basement creatures and fail to consider the role they play in keeping pest populations in check. “Our house is more peaceful now that it’s lurking down there. There are drawbacks, of course—my wife went down to do laundry the other day and hasn’t been the same since—but at least I don’t have to drop $500 on an exterminator. Sometimes you’ll step in a pool of bile and have to kick your shoes off before it burns through the soles, but that’s a small price to pay to not have rat droppings everywhere. And while it’s a little gross throwing out the larger and larger exoskeletons it keeps shedding, it’s still better than cleaning out a glue trap.” At press time, Burgess was hoping the rat problem would be solved for good now that he found two sets of smaller claw prints trailing the larger one.

title: Tether Pushes Back Against S&P as USDT Reserve Maintains Lowest Stability Assessment
description: Tether pushes back against S&P Global Ratings after the agency maintained its lowest stability assessment for USDT, pointing to a growing share of higher-risk assets in the stablecoin’s reserves and continuing concerns about transparency. In its latest assessment, published November 18, S&P kept USDT’s ability to maintain its dollar peg at 5 (weak), the lowest […]
fullContent:
Tether pushes back against S&P Global Ratings after the agency maintained its lowest stability assessment for USDT, pointing to a growing share of higher-risk assets in the stablecoin’s reserves and continuing concerns about transparency.

In its latest assessment, published November 18, S&P kept USDT’s ability to maintain its dollar peg at 5 (weak), the lowest score on its five-point scale. The rating remains unchanged from November 2025, when the agency first downgraded the stablecoin. Tether rejected the assessment, arguing that the problem lies with S&P’s evaluation framework rather than the composition of its reserves. The company also referenced The Big Short, the film about the 2008 financial crisis, in its response to the agency’s findings.

Higher-Risk Assets Account for 28% of USDT in Circulation

S&P’s latest concerns center on the changing composition of Tether’s reserves. According to the report, higher-risk holdings, including Bitcoin, gold, public equities, secured loans and corporate bonds, represented approximately 28% of USDT in circulation as of September 30.

That figure increased from 24% a year earlier, indicating a growing exposure to assets whose values can fluctuate with market conditions. S&P warned that a significant decline in the value of these holdings could leave USDT undercollateralized, particularly if several reserve assets experienced losses at the same time.

The company also argued that the agency’s own history demonstrated weaknesses in traditional financial risk assessments. Tether’s September 30 reserve report, attested by BDO, showed approximately $191.5 billion in assets against $183.5 billion in liabilities. This left the company with roughly $7.95 billion in excess assets.

S&P acknowledged the additional weaknesses identified in its review but did not lower the score further because 5 is already the bottom of its assessment scale.

S&P Questions Tether’s Regulatory Oversight and Reserve Safeguards

The agency also raised concerns about the regulatory framework governing Tether in El Salvador, where the company relocated in January 2025.

The country’s National Commission of Digital Assets requires 70% of reserves to be held in assets that can be liquidated within 30 days. However, S&P described the framework as broad, allowing assets such as Bitcoin, gold and loans to qualify despite their higher risk profiles.

Another concern involves the absence of a requirement to segregate reserve assets from the issuer’s other holdings. S&P noted that regulators in the United States and Europe generally expect stronger safeguards in this area. Without publicly available information confirming asset segregation, the agency said it could not determine how effectively USDT’s reserves are protected from broader corporate risks.

Tether’s Audit Disclosure Remains a Point of Contention

In August 2026, KPMG issued an unqualified opinion on Tether’s 2025 accounts, which the company described as its first full independent audit. Tether presented the development as support for its financial reporting. However, S&P said the audited financial statements and auditor’s report had not been published, limiting its ability to independently examine the underlying information.

The agency also highlighted that Tether’s reserve reports do not identify the custodians and counterparties holding its assets. Its attestations are published quarterly, while some competing stablecoin issuers provide monthly updates. Tether has challenged S&P’s assessments before. Following the initial downgrade in 2025, CEO Paolo Ardoino criticized the agency on X, saying the company wore its criticism with pride and pointing to previous financial collapses as evidence of weaknesses in traditional systems.

Despite maintaining the lowest rating, S&P acknowledged that USDT had demonstrated a strong record of price stability, particularly over the previous 12 months.

Can Tether address S&P’s concerns by improving reserve disclosures and reducing exposure to higher-risk assets? Will USDT’s established record of price stability continue to outweigh concerns about its reserve structure as the stablecoin market matures?

title: CLARITY Act Likely Dead Until 2027, Top Crypto Lawmakers Warn
description:
Bitcoin Magazine

CLARITY Act Likely Dead Until 2027, Top Crypto Lawmakers Warn
House Financial Services Chairman French Hill said the CLARITY Act's chances in the lame-duck session are "not high," pushing the crypto market structure bill toward a Democratic-led Congress.
This post CLARITY Act Likely Dead Until 2027, Top Crypto Lawmakers Warn first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.
fullContent:
Bitcoin Magazine

CLARITY Act Likely Dead Until 2027, Top Crypto Lawmakers Warn

House Financial Services Committee Chairman French Hill said the CLARITY Act is unlikely to pass before the year ends, leaving the crypto market structure bill to a new Congress that Democrats will control.

Hill spoke Thursday at the Capitol Crypto Forum in Washington. “We never give up hope in a lame duck, but it is lame, and therefore the chances are not high,” the Arkansas Republican said. He added that he plans to make market structure legislation his pitch in the next Congress, which begins in January.

“I regret that it was not something we could get done effectively in this Congress,” Hill said. He said 78 Democrats voted for the CLARITY Act in the House and that he expects that support to continue in the new Congress.

Hill also called it encouraging that Rep. Maxine Waters, the committee’s top Democrat, circulated a memo to House Democrats naming digital asset market structure as a topic she intends to work on if she becomes chair.

Senate floor time is running out

Sen. Bernie Moreno, the lead sponsor of the CLARITY Act in the Senate, told the same forum there is “no scenario” in which crypto legislation passes the chamber during the lame-duck session. Funding the government, the National Defense Authorization Act and the farm bill will take priority, according to The Hill, and the session is set to end in less than a month.

The Senate blocked the CLARITY Act on Sept. 15, voting 49-50 on a procedural motion that needed 60 votes. All Democrats and four Republicans opposed it, CBS News reported. Sen. Thom Tillis entered a motion to reconsider, which keeps the option of another vote alive, but the bill dies when this Congress ends Jan. 3 unless the lame-duck session revives it.

The House passed the legislation 294-134 in July 2025. President Donald Trump urged lawmakers in August to send it to his desk, but Democrats objected that its ethics provisions did not go far enough to address his potential conflicts of interest in crypto, and regulators have since moved ahead on their own, including an SEC exemption for tokenized stocks.

Democrats prepare to take over

The industry is now scrambling to repair its relationship with Democrats, Politico reported Thursday. The industry spent $55 million trying to defeat Sen.-elect Sherrod Brown of Ohio, who won his seat back, and Democrats are set to retake both the House and Senate in January.

Sen. Ruben Gallego, a crypto-friendly Arizona Democrat who spent months negotiating the Senate bill, gave Politico’s Jasper Goodman a blunt assessment of the industry’s political prospects. “They’re f***ed,” Gallego said, according to a post from journalist Eleanor Terrett.

Terrett has reported that House Democrats are discussing turning Waters’ Crypto Investor and Consumer Bill of Rights into their own market structure bill. The proposal would give the SEC a bigger role and the CFTC a smaller one, and she cited three industry sources who have spoken with Democratic staffers. Republicans have called it a “messaging bill.”

GENIUS Act deadline approaches

Hill used the forum to warn about the gap between the two bills. Trump signed the GENIUS Act, the stablecoin law, in July 2025, but market structure legislation never followed. Hill said the SEC and CFTC cannot fill the gap with exemptive relief alone, because it does not give the market lasting legal certainty. “When you pass GENIUS without CLARITY, it’s like passing and creating a cell phone, but you have no cell network,” Hill said.

The stablecoin law takes effect Jan. 18, 2027, and Treasury is still working on its rules. Terrett reported Wednesday that Sens. Cynthia Lummis and Kirsten Gillibrand, joined by four other senators, asked Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to extend a safe harbor to stablecoin issuers in states with rules in place before Jan. 18, 2028.

This post CLARITY Act Likely Dead Until 2027, Top Crypto Lawmakers Warn first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman.

The post Tom Brady Asks Candice Swanepoel If He Can Use Her Phone To Check Gisele’s Instagram  appeared first on The Onion.
fullContent:
INDIAN CREEK, FL—Promising he would be “real quick,” NFL commentator Tom Brady reportedly asked girlfriend Candice Swanepoel on Thursday if he could use her phone to check Gisele Bündchen’s Instagram. “You guys follow each other since you’re both models, right?” said the retired New England Patriots star, 49, adding that he would normally check Bündchen’s account using one of his kids’ phones, but they were no longer letting him. “I just want to peek at her story for a second. I promise I don’t still have feelings for her, babe. There’s just something I need to see. Come on, do this one thing for me? Great, thanks. And while I’m at it, do you mind if I use your account to send her a DM?” At press time, sources confirmed Brady was asking Swanepoel if he could use her phone a second time to check Peyton Manning’s account.

title: Bybit Joins Proof of Talk in Abu Dhabi 2026 as Title Partner and Official Exchange Partner
description: Bybit Joins Proof of Talk in Abu Dhabi 2026 as Title Partner and Official Exchange Partner
fullContent:
Dubai, United Arab Emirates, November 19th, 2026, Chainwire

Bybit, the New Financial Platform trusted by more than 80 million users worldwide, today announced its participation as Title Partner and Official Exchange Partner of Proof of Talk in Abu Dhabi 2026, taking place on December 3 and 4 at Louvre Abu Dhabi.

As part of the summit's programme, three Bybit executives will join discussions on the evolving financial landscape:

  • Ben Zhou, Co-founder and CEO of Bybit, will share perspectives on the evolution of digital asset exchanges into integrated financial platforms and the convergence of traditional and digital finance.
  • Sean Ballard, Head of Derivatives and Institutional Business at Bybit, will contribute insights on institutional liquidity, derivatives markets and trading infrastructure.
  • Derek Dai, MENA Country Manager at Bybit, will share regional insights on the future of finance, digital asset adoption and financial development across MENA.

Beyond the main summit, Bybit will also sponsor the Proof of Talk: Golf Prelude on December 2, bringing together a select group of founders, investors and industry leaders for an afternoon of networking ahead of the conference.

Hosted at Louvre Abu Dhabi, Proof of Talk marks its inaugural Gulf edition following four editions at the Louvre Palace in Paris. Organised by X Ventures, the invitation-only executive summit brings together senior decision-makers, institutional investors, financial leaders and technology innovators for discussions spanning capital, digital assets and artificial intelligence.

Bybit's participation builds on its growing presence in the UAE and its continued engagement with the country's regulatory framework. The company holds a full Virtual Asset Platform Operator Licence from the UAE Securities and Commodities Authority (SCA). In October 2026, Bybit also secured a Virtual Asset Service Provider (VASP) licence from Dubai's Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (VARA) for exchange services.

These milestones reflect Bybit's commitment to regulatory compliance and the responsible development of digital asset markets. The company sees the UAE as an important hub for connecting global financial opportunities with regional innovation, talent and institutional participation.

Through its partnership with Proof of Talk Abu Dhabi, Bybit looks forward to contributing to industry dialogue, strengthening relationships with regional and global stakeholders, and supporting the continued growth of the UAE as a centre for digital asset and financial innovation.

About Bybit

Bybit is The New Financial Platform.

We believe every person should have access to every financial opportunity on earth. That's why we're building the first intelligent platform that connects anyone, anywhere to the world's finance.

Trusted by more than 80 million users worldwide, Bybit brings together investing, trading, payments, and wealth-building in a single secure and intelligent ecosystem. Through the combination of AI-powered technology, deep global liquidity, robust security, and transparent operations, Bybit makes global finance more accessible, efficient, and empowering for everyone.

Built for everyone. Powered by intelligence. Open to the world.

Learn more at Bybit.com. 

For more details about Bybit, please visit Bybit Press

For media inquiries, please contact: media@bybit.com

For updates, please follow: Bybit's Communities and Social Media

title: 23 Million ADA Flow Back to Cardano's Treasury as the DJED Stablecoin Winds Down
description: Cardano's treasury took back 23 million ADA as the DJED stablecoin heads for shutdown. ADA looks oversold near $0.15, with $0.12 as the floor traders watch.
fullContent:
Quick Take

  • Cardano's treasury took back 23 million ADA from Project Catalyst as the DJED stablecoin heads toward shutdown.
  • ADA looks oversold on the daily chart, but momentum has not turned and sellers still control the trend.
  • Traders are watching the nearest support zone, the last clear floor before deeper losses.

Cardano's treasury received a large refund this week after Project Catalyst administration moved to the Cardano Foundation. The network is also preparing to retire DJED, its homegrown stablecoin, by the end of the year.

The two stories point the same way. Voters are tightening spending while a core DeFi product winds down, and ADA keeps sliding with the wider market. Traders now want to know whether buyers can defend the floor as DJED capital leaves.

Catalyst Hands 23 Million ADA Back to the Treasury

The refund came from Project Catalyst's Fund 15 and the Input Output Catalyst administration budget. Community tracker Cardanians said the funds returned after the administration change.

The transfer landed days after on-chain governance voted down a separate request. That proposal sought 22 million ADA to fund a copper tokenization project.

The two moves show voters guarding the treasury more closely. Money is flowing back in, and large asks are getting rejected. For a network that hands spending decisions to token holders, that marks a shift toward tighter budgets and more scrutiny of each proposal.

How We Got Here

DJED arrived in January 2023 as Cardano's answer to the stablecoin question. Input Output Global and COTI built it as an overcollateralized coin, backed by ADA and paired with a reserve token called SHEN.

Both tokens will now shut down on Dec. 31, 2026. The project urged holders to redeem, and told liquidity providers and lenders to withdraw their funds first. Redemptions will be honored until the cutoff.

Charles Hoskinson pushed back on talk of decline. He said on X that he "never once said Cardano is finished." On a podcast, he said he is moving from building Cardano to "building on Cardano."

Midnight, the privacy-focused sister chain, partnered with CD Security on elliptic-curve cryptography in zero-knowledge circuits. Its NIGHT token traded near $0.04, up about 16% over 30 days.

Half the October Value Gone and $0.12 Is the Last Floor

Cardano (ADA) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

ADA trades near $0.15, roughly half its early-October peak of about $0.30. The coin fell about 13% over the past week and around 30% over the month. The whole market fell. Bitcoin briefly slipped under $62,000, Ethereum dropped below $1,800 and XRP lost the $1 mark.

The trend still favors sellers. ADA sits below its 50-day average near $0.19. It also trades under its 200-day average near $0.22. Both lines now act as ceilings, and trend strength readings confirm sellers are leading a real move lower.

RSI, a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, reads 29. That puts ADA in oversold territory, so the drop looks stretched. Momentum has not turned yet, though, and the MACD still points down.

Support sits near $0.12, with no clear floor below it. Buyers would need to reclaim $0.18 and then $0.20 to change the picture. Analyst Lana Valentis said she is watching the midline of a descending weekly channel.

A Leaner Cardano Trades Its Stablecoin for Discipline

  • The project: It loses its only native overcollateralized stablecoin, a gap for DeFi apps that relied on DJED. In return, the treasury is fuller, and voters have shown they will reject large spending requests.
  • DJED and SHEN holders: They must redeem before the year-end cutoff. Liquidity providers and lenders need to pull funds first, or they risk being left with tokens that no longer work.
  • ADA holders: The cleanup offers no immediate lift to the price. The coin's market value has shrunk to about $5.8 billion, leaving it ranked 18th among cryptocurrencies.

Will Redemptions Run Smoothly Into Year End?

The DJED unwind is the next test for Cardano.

  • Redemption pace: Steady, orderly redemptions would show the shutdown is under control. A late rush could strain liquidity pools.
  • DeFi outflows: Lenders and liquidity providers pulling funds will thin Cardano's DeFi activity.
  • The floor: ADA needs to hold its nearest support while that capital leaves.

fullContent:
As CEO and co-founder of the AI juggernaut Anthropic, Dario Amodei has helped shape the conversation surrounding the technology’s future and potential risks. The Onion sat down with the tech titan to discuss what comes next for Anthropic and AI writ large.

The Onion : How do you pronounce your last name?

Amodei: That’s the kind of decision I leave up to Claude.

What is the best way to explain artificial intelligence to a nonexpert?

It’s like when a dog looks in a mirror and thinks he’s seeing another dog.

What makes Claude different?

I’m gonna use a lot of words, sentences, and a lot of terms, which are also words but more specific, to distract, divert you, as in you, from the fact that it’s not really that different at all.

How much are you making from Anthropic’s IPO?

It’s a number you’re too poor to have heard of.

What do you consider the biggest technological breakthrough of our time?

TiVo.

What about your work scares you the most?

Partiful invites from Elon.

Will AI destroy humanity?

Only if we don’t like the same sports team as it.

Do you know if spies have approached you?

Everyone in my harem says no.

Are you involved in any charities?

I’m a major backer of initiatives to provide cardigans to weird little boys.

What do you do for fun?

I like to DM Sam Altman on my burner accounts to tell him he looks like a bag of milk.

What is your ultimate goal with Anthropic?

We want Claude to be the sophisticated, professional voice behind every failed startup in the country.

title: US Launches Crypto Crime Center With TRM Labs to Track Scams, Stolen Funds
description: The US launches Crypto Crime Center, a new initiative to disrupt criminal networks behind online scams, cybercrime, and cryptocurrency theft, bringing together federal investigators, state and local agencies, financial institutions, and technology companies. The newly established Threat Disruption Center aims to shorten the time between a victim reporting a crime and authorities taking action to […]
fullContent:
The US launches Crypto Crime Center, a new initiative to disrupt criminal networks behind online scams, cybercrime, and cryptocurrency theft, bringing together federal investigators, state and local agencies, financial institutions, and technology companies.

The newly established Threat Disruption Center aims to shorten the time between a victim reporting a crime and authorities taking action to trace and potentially freeze stolen funds. The initiative will involve more than 30 federal agencies and over 440 state and local partners. Blockchain analytics company TRM Labs has been selected to provide the center’s primary investigative technology under a federal contract worth $94.66 million.

The launch comes as cryptocurrency-related fraud continues to generate substantial losses. The FBI recorded more than $11 billion in reported losses involving cryptocurrency during 2025, highlighting the need for faster coordination between investigators and private-sector platforms.

Threat Disruption Center Brings Agencies and Crypto Platforms Together

The Threat Disruption Center will operate as a shared investigative resource, allowing law enforcement agencies to exchange information with participating companies as they identify victims, trace transactions and investigate criminal networks.

The approach is intended to help authorities intervene before scammers move stolen funds beyond recovery. Cryptocurrency exchanges and payment providers may be able to stop transfers or freeze assets, while social media companies can remove accounts used to contact and deceive victims.

Law enforcement agencies will continue conducting investigations and pursuing court-authorized asset seizures as part of the broader effort. John A. Condon, acting executive associate director of Homeland Security Investigations, said the partnerships would help authorities identify and dismantle criminal networks more quickly, disrupt fraud at its source and protect potential victims.

The center also reflects a broader effort to strengthen cooperation between government agencies and private companies as online fraud becomes increasingly organized across international borders.

According to the FBI’s 2025 Internet Crime Report, the bureau received 181,565 complaints involving cryptocurrency. Crypto investment fraud accounted for approximately $7.2 billion of the more than $11 billion in reported cryptocurrency-related losses. The FBI has also identified criminal networks operating in Southeast Asia among those responsible for many of these schemes. Some operations involve trafficked individuals who are forced to participate in fraudulent activities.

TRM Labs Secures $94.66 Million Contract for Investigative Technology

TRM Labs will provide Ardence as the Threat Disruption Center’s primary investigative platform. The technology will help investigators process victim complaints, trace cryptocurrency transactions and map the networks responsible for fraudulent activity.

Government procurement records show that TRM Labs received a $94.66 million contract in July to support the initiative. The agreement is scheduled to run through August 29, 2027. The company will supply the technology and investigative capabilities needed to support cooperation between participating agencies and private-sector partners.

By connecting transaction data with information about criminal networks, investigators aim to identify where stolen assets are moving and determine whether intervention is still possible. The platform is also intended to help authorities identify connections between separate complaints, potentially revealing larger operations that target multiple victims through similar methods.

FBI’s Operation Level Up Provides a Foundation for the Initiative

The Threat Disruption Center builds on existing government efforts to identify cryptocurrency fraud victims and prevent additional losses.

One example is Operation Level Up, an FBI initiative launched in 2024 to identify people targeted by cryptocurrency investment scams and warn them before they send additional money to criminals.

According to the bureau, the operation has notified more than 8,000 victims and helped prevent over $500 million in losses. The new center expands the scope of this approach by bringing more agencies and private-sector companies into a shared operational framework.

For the cryptocurrency industry, the development highlights the growing importance of cooperation between exchanges, analytics providers and law enforcement agencies. Faster information-sharing could help limit fraud-related losses, although the effectiveness of the new center will ultimately depend on how quickly participating organizations can act and how often stolen funds can actually be recovered.

Will the Threat Disruption Center significantly reduce cryptocurrency-related fraud by enabling faster intervention? Could closer cooperation between US authorities and crypto platforms lead to stronger expectations for exchanges and other digital asset service providers?

title: Hong Kong SFC Flags Hyperliquid as a Suspicious Trading Platform
description:
Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) has added Hyperliquid to its list of suspicious virtual asset trading platforms, saying the platform is not licensed to provide services in the city. 
This is not the first time a financial regulator has flagged Hyperliquid. In May, the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) urged people to stay away from the platform, saying it "may be providing or promoting financial services or products without our permission". 
Onchain Architecture Does Not Offer Immunity
In its warning published on 18 November, the regulator said Hyperliquid may be actively marketing its services to local investors, but accounts and assets held through Hyperliquid are outside the supervision applied to SFC-licensed platforms. 
The regulator also warned that clients of unlicensed platforms could lose their holdings if an operator collapses, stops trading, is hacked, or misappropriates assets.  The notice covers Hyperliquid at the platform level, without separately addressing spot and perpetual products. 
 Hong Kong’s licensing rules apply to platforms operating in Hong Kong and to overseas companies that target  Hong Kong investors. Thus, offshore registration or an on-chain trading model does not automatically place a platform outside the local regulatory perimeter.
What Other Platforms Should Check 
When assessing financial platforms, regulators review more than just the legal address. They will look at whether the crypto platform, the broker, the wallet and the trading venue will allow onboarding, whether they will run local advertising and whether they will have a referral programme. 
Companies also need to look at the permissions by product. A licence to trade virtual assets doesn't necessarily cover derivative style contracts or all the associated services.
Under the HK Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance, it is a criminal offence to actively market unlicensed virtual asset services to the HK public. Such activity may lead to access blocking orders, banking restrictions and enforcement against the local promoter or affiliates.


This article was written by Tanya Chepkova at www.financemagnates.com.

title: Solana Is Planning Its Next Major Upgrades: Here’s What Changes
description: There are plans to replace Turbine with Rotor, a flatter block-distribution system intended to cut latency across the entire Solana network.
fullContent:
Solana is getting ready for another round of network upgrades in 2027, with plans to double compute capacity and cut the compute units needed by token accounts by 80%.

A roadmap unveiled by Anza CEO Brennan Watt also includes faster block distribution, changes to transaction ordering, and cheaper on-chain computation, as developers look to accommodate more demanding financial applications.

Solana Plans Major Network Overhaul in 2027

In a video shared by Solana on November 19, Watt outlined the roadmap across several areas, including performance, expressivity, market structure, and resilience. The plans are a continuation of what has been a busy year for core development on the network, culminating in the recent migration from Tower BFT to its new consensus protocol, Alpenglow.

As Watt noted, Solana has already cut block times from 400 milliseconds to 200 milliseconds while also doubling performance to about 250 million compute units (CUs) per second. With the move to Alpenglow, the time required for transaction finality also dropped by a wide margin, from 12.8 seconds to roughly 150 milliseconds.

For next year, the team wants to overhaul the network’s storage backend and rewrite its associated token account program. According to Watt, the latter should cut down by 80% the CUs used by token-account operations. Furthermore, he said the anticipated storage changes should allow validators to handle more data and process additional activity without disrupting existing applications.

“Several important Alpenglow extensions are coming, including optimizing the leader handoffs by better pipelining it and bringing geographical awareness in-protocol,” Watt said, describing the round of changes expected for networking. The team also plans to replace Solana’s existing block-distribution system, Turbine, with a flatter protocol called Rotor designed to cut down network latency.

Another proposed upgrade called Constellation will change how blocks are assembled. According to Watt, it will feature a faster market tick and transparent rules for the ordering of transactions as well as a second proposer. He said that the introduction of a second proposer should bring competition among validators to include transactions.

Adding Room for On-Chain Financial Apps

The roadmap also addressed computational limits that have been restricting some complex applications on Solana.

“We’re making hardcore computation viable on-chain, opening the door for fully on-chain options pricing and sophisticated margin models,” said the Anza executive.

He added that cheaper math would support “richer financial logic,” which he believes will complement Solana’s dominance in spot trading. Additionally, the team wants to make it possible for devs to read account data instead of copying it and, in that way, reduce the amount of information that needs to move during execution.

These plans are being made with Solana attracting activity beyond speculative trading, as revealed by a report last month from Castle Labs, which showed the network’s tokenized real-world assets had gone from about $700 million to well over $4 billion in just one year.

That said, the network’s native SOL token has struggled alongside the wider crypto market. Data from CoinGecko at the time of writing showed it trading near $75, a nearly 30% drop in the last 30 days and 46% lower than where it was 12 months ago. Its $293 all-time high is also not under any threat of being matched or surpassed, with the current price representing a dip of more than 70% from that level.

description: Ethereum is attempting to stabilize around $1.8K after a steep November sell-off that erased the asset’s entire August rally.
