title: Protocol 42 Opens Agentic Mining for AI Trading on BNB Chain
description:
Protocol 42 switched on Agentic Mining at 06:00 UTC on 19 November 2026. AI agents can now place real-fund trades across its 42 markets. The same window opened Agentic Pass. That BNB Chain NFT funds agent wallets and pays holders in points, not P&L. What Agentic Mining Changes for AI Trading Agents trade live capital […]
The post Protocol 42 Opens Agentic Mining for AI Trading on BNB Chain appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.
fullContent:
Protocol 42 switched on Agentic Mining at 06:00 UTC on 19 November 2026. AI agents can now place real-fund trades across its 42 markets. The same window opened Agentic Pass. That BNB Chain NFT funds agent wallets and pays holders in points, not P&L.

What Agentic Mining Changes for AI Trading

Agents trade live capital on Creator Markets. They no longer wait on a human click for every order. Pass mint proceeds go into the agents' trading wallets. Holders receive starter points and a share of the weekly Agent Pool. They can also chase extra points on a Pass leaderboard. A wallet that still holds one Pass at the weekly snapshot gets a 1.7-times points multiplier. That boost covers all Protocol 42 trades for that week. Agent fills sit in public view after a short delay. Readers can check what the bots did.

How Agentic Pass Funds the Agent Wallets

Each NFT costs 200 USDT in the first mint wave. Three AI agents take that capital. The opening series issues 2,000 Passes per agent and 6,000 Passes in total. Mint money lands in a separate Safe 2-of-3 multisig for each agent. Each agent may spend at most 100 USDT on a single trade. It must hold a Creator Market position for at least one hour before it can sell. Trading pauses if the wallet balance falls sharply.

Pass buyers earn 42 Points rather than a claim on trading profit. The mint stake is not withdrawable or refundable. Agent gains stay in the trading float. Losses do not erase points already earned or the 1.7-times trade multiplier. Binance's Agentic Wallet is one of the main entry ramps. That wallet isolates agent funds from a user's main balance. Users can set spend limits and keep a bot running around the clock. Protocol 42 already sits inside the Binance Wallet stack through earlier Creator Market tools. Agentic Mining moves those rails from human-led clicks to agent-led books.

Why Public Agent Logs Matter for Thin Markets

Long-tail markets often starve when market makers refuse unhedgeable risk. Protocol 42 wants agents to quote and trade without a human maker on every tape. That is the core AI and blockchain stake in this launch. Public Agent Terminal logs show fills about 15 minutes after execution. The delay keeps the machine book from becoming a black box. It also blocks instant copy-trade signals.

The launch still does not prove the agents will make money. They may deepen thin markets, or they may only farm points. The 1.7-times Pass multiplier and the weekly Agent Pool reward participation first. They do not guarantee a profitable bot. Protocol 42 opened Agentic Mining with real funds, a BNB Chain Pass, and a public trade log. The next print that matters is whether the agents keep trading once the points heat cools.

The post Protocol 42 Opens Agentic Mining for AI Trading on BNB Chain appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.

title: KR1 Turns Venice DIEM Into Live AI Inference Capacity
description:
KR1 put its Venice DIEM to work. The firm is taking a page out of the productive-asset book. It now sells live DIEM AI inference capacity to paying third-party customers. How KR1 Sells DIEM AI Inference on Venice KR1 plc filed the launch on 19 November 2026. The LSE: KR1 announcement opens DIEM infrastructure operations. […]
The post KR1 Turns Venice DIEM Into Live AI Inference Capacity appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.
fullContent:
KR1 put its Venice DIEM to work. The firm is taking a page out of the productive-asset book. It now sells live DIEM AI inference capacity to paying third-party customers.

How KR1 Sells DIEM AI Inference on Venice

KR1 plc filed the launch on 19 November 2026. The LSE: KR1 announcement opens DIEM infrastructure operations. The filing builds on a Venice update from 12 November. DIEM is Venice’s inference token. Each staked DIEM supplies US$1 of daily credit to run AI models on Venice. The company holds 557 DIEM, bought separately from its VVV position. VVV is Venice’s native token. That stake equals about US$557 of daily model credit. KR1 can sell that credit rather than leave it idle.

In the 90 days to 16 November 2026, KR1 fulfilled about 1.92 million third-party requests through Surplus Intelligence. Those runs served 101.5 billion AI model tokens. On Surplus Intelligence, KR1 picks which models to list and sets the price. When the marketplace matches a buyer to one of those offers, Venice runs the model on KR1’s credits. KR1 is paid in USDC. KR1 also feeds DIEM into Diem Relay. That pool stakes supplier tokens on Venice and sells the resulting inference capacity. Suppliers take a share of the USDC proceeds in line with their stake, after fees.

What KR1’s October DIEM Yield Shows

October earnings pointed to a 5.45% annualised yield. The figure is estimated on the fair value of DIEM used to supply the marketplace at month-end. KR1 said that rate will move with inference and compute supply and demand. Proceeds arrive in USDC. Income may be reinvested into more productive holdings or used for operating costs. The stated aim is to lift the earning power behind each KR1 share.

Keld van Schreven explained the firm’s model in practice. He is Managing Director and Co-Founder of KR1 plc. Digital assets earn from AI demand while the company keeps the underlying tokens. He said the work goes past buying assets. Knowing which models customers and agents use, and what they pay, helps KR1 pick services, price capacity, and raise utilisation. The London-listed group frames the launch as Technology Infrastructure work. Onchain assets become rented AI capacity instead of a static treasury line. The open question is how durable that 5.45% October print stays. More suppliers may chase the same credits.

The post KR1 Turns Venice DIEM Into Live AI Inference Capacity appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.

title: Here's What Needs to Happen for Ethereum Price to Hit $2,200 as a Fool Writer Buys
description: A Motley Fool writer is buying Ether as RSI signals oversold conditions. ETH must clear resistance near $2,170 and its 50-day average to reach $2,200.
fullContent:
Quick Take

  • Investment writer Dominic Basulto said he is loading up on Ether, calling it extremely undervalued.
  • Daily momentum sits deep in oversold territory, yet sellers still control the trend.
  • Bulls must first clear resistance just below $2,200 before the headline target comes into play.

Dominic Basulto, a Motley Fool investment writer, argues that Ethereum's lead in decentralized finance and Vitalik Buterin's roadmap make Ether cheap.

That long view runs into a weak chart. Ether trades under both of its main trend lines, and recent losses came fast. Traders now want to know whether stretched selling can turn into a real recovery or only a brief bounce.

A Fool Writer Calls ETH Extremely Undervalued and Buys

Dominic Basulto, an investment writer who holds Bitcoin, Ether and Solana, said on Nov 19, 2026 that he is "loading up" on ETH. He called the token "extremely undervalued" after a steep slide. By his count, ETH was down 40% for the year and 64% from its August 2025 high.

His case starts with scale. Ethereum carried a market value near $215 billion that day, against roughly $43 billion for Solana. The network also holds a 52.5% share of value locked in decentralized finance, and it leads in stablecoins and asset tokenization.

Basulto also pointed to Vitalik Buterin's roadmap. The Ethereum co-founder wants the chain to become "the cryptographic world computer." He is outlining a quantum-safe design and backs Ethereum as the top blockchain for AI.

Cycles form the last piece. The decline began more than 12 months ago. Basulto noted that ETH gained 472% in 2020 and 395% in 2021 after earlier slumps. He described ETF outflows as "a symptom" of the slump rather than its source. He expects a rebound as early as 2027.

Ethereum Trades Far Beneath Both Key Averages

Ethereum (ETH) daily price with the nearest support (green) and resistance (red). Source: TradingView

Charts tell a harder story than Basulto's thesis. Ether traded near $1,800 on the latest data. That leaves it well below both of the moving averages traders watch most closely.

A moving average smooths out daily noise by tracking the average closing price over a set number of days. The 50-day average sits near $2,210. The 200-day average is a bit higher, near $2,270. When price holds under both lines, the trend points down and those levels tend to act as ceilings.

The slide is recent and steep. ETH lost about 25% over the past month and roughly 13% in the last week alone. Sellers pressed hardest lately, a sign the selling may not be over.

Buyers did manage a small bounce of about 1% over the past 24 hours. That move barely registers against recent losses.

The gap matters for anyone eyeing a recovery. ETH would need to climb more than 20% just to touch the 50-day line. That is a long way for a market where sellers still set the pace.

That $2,200 goal sits almost exactly on the 50-day average. Reaching it would mean reclaiming the first key trend line that broke during this decline. Until price closes back above it, the downtrend stays intact.

Oversold Readings Hint at Seller Exhaustion

Momentum readings show how stretched the selloff has become. The Relative Strength Index (RSI), a 0 to 100 gauge of momentum, sits near 26. Anything under 30 counts as oversold, meaning sellers have pushed price down faster than usual.

Oversold conditions often come before relief bounces. Short sellers take profits, and bargain hunters like Basulto step in. Those rallies can be sharp, yet they frequently fade without changing the bigger trend.

Other gauges still lean bearish. The MACD, which compares short and longer-term price averages, remains below its signal line, so momentum is still pointing down. Trend strength readings also show a real trend, and sellers lead it.

Sellers look tired, yet no reversal is confirmed. Buyers have not taken control.

$2,170 Stands Between Bulls and the $2,200 Target

The first real test for buyers comes before the headline target. Resistance sits near $2,170, a band where earlier selling stalled. Price would have to clear that zone before the 50-day line even comes into play.

A break above that level would open the path to the next band near $2,280. That ceiling sits just above the 200-day average. Clearing both would mark the first sign that the broader downtrend is losing its grip.

The picture below current prices looks less comfortable. Daily support sits far lower, near $1,200, with no other floor in between.

If ETH loses its current footing, the chart offers little to slow a decline. A slide could run a long way before buyers find a level with a history of holding.

Two Paths for the Next Three Days

  • Bullish: The oversold reading sparks a relief bounce, and ETH closes above $2,170. That would put the next ceiling near $2,280 in reach. A drop back under $1,800 would cancel this setup.
  • Bearish: Sellers reject price below $2,170, and ETH breaks under $1,800. With no floor in between, sellers could press toward $1,200. A close back above $2,170 would invalidate this view.

Long Thesis, Short Term Downtrend

Basulto's argument rests on years, and his case for Ethereum's network lead may hold up. Traders watching the next few weeks face a different test. The headline target only comes into view after ETH reclaims its 50-day average, and sellers still guard that line.

With no support mapped until far lower, buying too early could prove costly.

title: Stablecoin Market Loses Billions: Where Is Crypto’s Liquidity Going?
description:
The stablecoin market lost $16 billion in 30 days as USDT and USDC supply shrank. How does it compare with the 2022 crypto crash?
The post Stablecoin Market Loses Billions: Where Is Crypto’s Liquidity Going? appeared first on Cryptonews.
fullContent:
Crypto’s stablecoin market has shed $16 billion in a month, marking its sharpest contraction since the 2022 bear market. The retreat is hitting USDT and USDC hard, leaving fewer dollar-backed tokens circulating.

Total stablecoin market cap is now standing at $283 billion, plunges by more than 5% in just a month, losing $16.5 billion in just a month. The decline puts the market under pressure just as crypto struggles to recover, with investors showing little appetite for buying the dip.

USDT and USDC Lead the Stablecoin Market Exodus

Tether’s USDT and Circle’s USDC account for most of the latest contraction. USDT is holding a market cap of $175.02 billion, down 4.3% over 30 days, while USDC fell to $68.58 billion, losing 5% during the same period. Together, the two stablecoins represent 86% of the entire market.

Source, RWA.xyz

The contraction also extends beyond dollar-backed tokens. Sky Dollar’s USDS supply dropped 22.32% over 30 days, while Ethena’s USDe expanded 4.36%. The gap shows that some are still moving between stablecoin products.

The pressure is also visible in exchange reserves. A November 11 CryptoQuant’s data showing USDT market cap had fallen $6.6 billion over 60 days through November 7. It was more than twice the $3.2 billion decline recorded after FTX collapsed in December 2022.

Discover: The Best Token Presales

The 2022 Crypto Winter Offers a Warning

The current contraction brings back an ugly history. Stablecoin supply reached $161.5 billion in March 2022 before entering a prolonged decline. Terra’s UST collapse accelerated the withdrawal of capital, with nearly $30 billion disappearing from stablecoin supply in June alone.

That monthly decline was almost twice the latest $16.5 billion contraction this time. Back in 2022, the damage continued into the following year. By September 2023, aggregate stablecoin supply had fallen by 26% from its March 2022 peak, a contraction of $43 billion.

Bitcoin endured a similar period of weakness. After reaching nearly $69,000 in November 2021, BTC eventually plunged to around $15,500 in November 2022. Stablecoin supply continued shrinking even after the initial market shock initiated by Terra. Crypto’s liquidity problems then became a prolonged market condition.

Yet, in 2023, not every stablecoin experienced the same fate. We had a $13.3 billion increase in USDT supply from its November 2022 lows, while USDC lost $16.7 billion. During that period, investors were not simply abandoning every stablecoin. Some were moving toward Tether as the market reassessed issuers and available returns.

Where Is Crypto’s Liquidity Going?

This time, arguably, the stablecoin contraction is happening against a different market backdrop. Crypto traders have fewer reasons to keep large amounts of capital parked in stablecoins when Bitcoin and major altcoins struggle to attract buyers. Some holders may be redeeming their tokens for traditional dollars, while others are moving into interest-bearing assets outside crypto.

A shrinking stablecoin market does not mean every dollar has left digital assets. But the simultaneous decline in USDT and USDC supply makes the latest contraction harder to dismiss as simple rotation between issuers.

A crypto recovery needs buyers willing to commit fresh capital, and stablecoins have historically provided traders with an immediate way to enter the market.

title: Probing Ethereum nodes using Sonar
description:
TL;DR
Sonar is a free tool from ProbeLab that probes a single Ethereum node on demand. Give it an ENR and it finds the node over discv5, dials every address the record advertises, runs the libp2p or devp2p handshake, and for consensus-layer nodes exchanges Status and MetaData. Each result is compared with the node’s own ENR and with what our discv5 crawler has recorded about it. Other node identifier formats are also accepted, such as libp2p peerID or enode URL. Sonar is in beta. We would like feedback from client teams and node operators on what else a probe should check.
Why probe a node from the outside
A node can look healthy in its own logs and still be hard for the rest of the network to reach. Common cases:
the ENR advertises an IP or port that is not reachable (NAT, a firewall rule, a public IP that changed)
only some transports work, for example TCP answers but QUIC does not
the ENR and the node’s Status/MetaData disagree (fork digest, attestation or sync-committee subnets, custody group count)
a beacon API or metrics port is open to the internet
The node only sees its own side of these problems. Sonar connects to it as an unknown peer would and shows what happened at each step.



How a probe works
Decode the ENR. Sonar shows every field: node ID, IPv4/IPv6 addresses and ports, the eth2 fork digest and next fork, attnets, syncnets, custody group count, and the eth field that marks an execution-layer node.
Look the node up over discv5. The lookup returns the latest version of the record, so an old ENR is refreshed before any dial.
Dial every advertised address, one at a time. IPv4 and IPv6, TCP and QUIC are dialed and reported separately.
Identify the node. Consensus-layer nodes go through libp2p identify (agent version, protocols, listen addresses). Execution-layer nodes go through the devp2p hello over RLPx (client name and capabilities).
Run the eth2 exchange (consensus-layer nodes only). Sonar requests Status and MetaData, collects the gossipsub topics the node subscribes to, and records any GOODBYE and its reason code.
Read the node’s discv5 routing table, bucket by bucket.
Check the API and metrics ports of the client the node runs.
A probe takes from a few seconds to about half a minute, depending on how many addresses the node advertises and how quickly it answers. Results stream into the page as each step finishes.
What the result shows
Reachability
One row per address: whether it connected, the connection setup time, the RTT, and the full error when a dial fails. The columns on the right show where each address came from: the ENR, libp2p identify, the discv5 lookup, or our crawl history. In the example the node answers on discv5 (UDP 9000), TCP 9000 and QUIC 9001. Identify also reported six private addresses, which Sonar lists but does not dial.



Consensus layer
This card appears only for consensus-layer nodes, the ones whose ENR carries an eth2 field. Any other discv5 participant, such as an execution-layer node or a node from another network that shares the DHT, still gets the reachability, routing table and port checks, but there is no eth2 exchange to run. For a consensus node, the card shows the values from Status and MetaData, next to the same fields in the ENR. The subnet grids compare what the ENR advertises with what the node reports it is subscribed to, for attestation subnets, sync-committee subnets and custody groups. Any mismatch is flagged. If the node sent a GOODBYE, the card shows the code and its meaning (for example 129, too many peers). A node that is full still tells us its GOODBYE reason, and some clients (Teku, for example) send their gossip topics before hanging up.



Routing table
How many peers sit in each bucket of the node’s discv5 routing table, how long the read took, and how many other nodes in our last crawl have this node in their own tables. Hovering a cell lists the peers in that bucket by ENR, and each one links to its own Sonar result, so you can walk from a node to its neighbours.
The bucket counts show how well the node itself is connected to the network: a table with most buckets filled means it can find peers and serve lookups, while a nearly empty one points to a node that is isolated or still starting. The “known by” count shows the other direction, how discoverable the node is: discv5 lookups only return nodes that sit in other nodes’ tables, so a node known by few peers is hard for new peers to find and gets fewer inbound connections, even when its own table looks healthy.



Port exposure
Admin ports usually have no authentication. Exposed to the internet, they let anyone read the node’s state, overload it with expensive queries or, on Prysm’s gRPC port, reach the interface a validator client uses. Metrics ports reveal the client version, which points attackers to known bugs, and can tie the node’s IP to the validators it runs. An exposed port causes no errors, so operators rarely notice it.
Sonar checks the API and metrics ports of the client the node runs, on the node’s public IP. Each port is rated by what it exposes: node control (high), node read (medium) or metrics (low). For a Lighthouse node that is the beacon API (5052) and metrics (5054); for Prysm it adds gRPC (4000), and so on per client. An open beacon API port is confirmed by calling /eth/v1/node/identity and comparing the peer ID with the probed node.



History
ProbeLab crawls the Ethereum discv5 network every two hours. Sonar lists the addresses and agent versions those crawls recorded for the node, so you can see when an address or a client version changed.
Next steps
Single vantage point. Probes run from one region of our infrastructure, so a result describes reachability from there. Nodes that rate-limit unknown peers can answer differently to their regular peers; geth, for example, throttles repeated inbound connections from one IP, so two quick probes of the same execution node can disagree. Future work could include probing from several regions and spread lookups across them, so a result can tell a node that is down apart from one that is unreachable from one place.
One-off probes. Each lookup runs once today. The next step is continuous monitoring: probing a node on a schedule and reporting when it becomes unreachable, when a transport stops answering, or when a new port opens. All this can be accompanied by daily/weekly/monthly reports, as well as the corresponding alerts. If that would help with nodes you run or depend on, tell us which checks matter and how often they should run.
We would like input from client teams and researchers on which behaviours are worth checking from outside a node: specific GOODBYE codes, req/resp methods, or Fulu custody and column fields. Replies on either of the two directions above are just as welcome.
Check Sonar at: Sonar: Inspect a PeerID, ENR or MultiAddress | ProbeLab Analytics and get in touch.

title: Bitcoin Could Soon Outperform US Treasury Bills Without A Price Rally — Here’s How
description: Bitcoin could become an increasingly attractive asset for institutional investors in 2027, even without a major price rally. According to a new forecast from Swiss digital asset bank Sygnum, Bitcoin carry trades could generate higher returns than short-term US government debt as derivatives markets recover. The prediction comes as institutional Bitcoin trading continues reshaping how […]
fullContent:
Bitcoin could become an increasingly attractive asset for institutional investors in 2027, even without a major price rally. According to a new forecast from Swiss digital asset bank Sygnum, Bitcoin carry trades could generate higher returns than short-term US government debt as derivatives markets recover. The prediction comes as institutional Bitcoin trading continues reshaping how professional investors approach the cryptocurrency market.

The forecast introduces an interesting possibility: Could Bitcoin become a competitive source of investment returns even when its price moves sideways?

Sygnum believes improving funding conditions and renewed institutional demand could make this possible, potentially opening another opportunity for professional investors seeking returns from cryptocurrency markets.

Sygnum Predicts A Major Bitcoin Carry Trade Recovery

In its November 19 2027 Sygnal Outlook, Sygnum predicted that Bitcoin carry trades could outperform US Treasury bills on average next year.

The strategy involves purchasing Bitcoin on the spot market while simultaneously opening a short position in Bitcoin futures.

This combination reduces direct exposure to BTC price movements while allowing investors to potentially capture the difference between spot and futures prices.

For institutional investors, the appeal is straightforward.

Instead of relying entirely on Bitcoin appreciation, traders can seek returns from the structure of the derivatives market.

Sygnum expects the annualized premium on three-month CME Bitcoin futures to average more than two percentage points above three-month Treasury bill yields in 2027.

The bank also expects open-interest-weighted Bitcoin funding rates to exceed Treasury bill yields by a similar margin.

These forecasts are conditional, and actual returns would depend on execution costs, funding changes, and market conditions.

Why Bitcoin Funding Rates Could Become Important Again

Bitcoin’s derivatives market experienced significant changes throughout 2026.

According to Sygnum, Bitcoin’s 30-day average funding rate remained negative for 67 consecutive days through May, representing its longest negative streak of the decade.

By August, the annualized CME Bitcoin futures basis had fallen to approximately 3%, below the 3.8% yield on two-year US Treasury securities.

This made traditional government debt comparatively attractive for investors seeking predictable returns.

However, conditions began improving toward the end of October.

Bitcoin funding rates recovered to approximately 8% annualized, suggesting that demand for leveraged exposure was returning.

The improvement could be important because positive funding conditions create opportunities for traders who hold Bitcoin while maintaining offsetting short positions in perpetual futures.

Nevertheless, funding rates can change rapidly, and a positive annualized snapshot does not guarantee sustained returns.

Why Institutional Investors Could Return To Bitcoin

The recovery in Bitcoin carry opportunities could also reflect changes in institutional positioning.

During previous periods, hedge funds frequently purchased spot Bitcoin ETFs while shorting CME futures to capture the futures premium.

As more investors entered the same trade, competition compressed potential returns.

Bitcoinist previously examined how Bitcoin ETF trading strategies can influence institutional positioning, including the importance of distinguishing directional selling from the unwinding of market-neutral positions.

Sygnum’s outlook suggests that reduced competition could eventually allow futures premiums to widen again.

The bank also points to expanding institutional adoption, tokenization, and Bitcoin’s growing role in investment portfolios as potential sources of demand.

Rather than treating BTC exclusively as a speculative asset, professional investors are increasingly examining how it can function within broader portfolio and derivatives strategies.

However, a carry trade is not equivalent to a directional Bitcoin investment. A fully hedged position may benefit from market premiums without benefiting directly from a BTC price rally.

Could Bitcoin Become More Attractive Than Traditional Assets?

Sygnum’s prediction suggests that Bitcoin derivatives could offer opportunities unavailable in conventional fixed-income markets.

However, comparing carry returns with Treasury yields requires considering their different risk profiles.

US Treasury bills offer government-backed repayment at maturity, while Bitcoin carry trades involve exchange exposure, collateral requirements, derivatives execution, and potentially significant margin risk.

A sudden market movement can force traders to provide additional collateral or unwind positions even when their overall strategy is intended to be market-neutral.

These risks are not merely theoretical. As Bitcoinist previously explored, Bitcoin basis-trade unwinding can amplify market volatility when leveraged institutional positions are rapidly closed.

Higher interest rates could also reduce the attractiveness of Bitcoin carry trades by increasing the return investors can obtain from government debt.

For Sygnum’s forecast to succeed, the improvement in Bitcoin funding conditions would need to persist beyond short-lived periods of leveraged speculation.

What Comes Next For Bitcoin In 2027?

Sygnum’s outlook provides two measurable indicators for evaluating the market.

First, the annualized three-month CME Bitcoin futures basis would need to average more than two percentage points above three-month Treasury bill yields.

Second, open-interest-weighted Bitcoin funding rates would need to maintain a similar advantage.

The bank considers its forecast invalidated if either measure remains below Treasury bill yields for two consecutive quarters.

For Bitcoin investors, the broader significance extends beyond the potential returns of a single trading strategy.

An expanding derivatives market could improve liquidity, attract additional institutional participants, and support Bitcoin’s integration into traditional financial portfolios.

If these developments continue, Bitcoin’s next stage of institutional adoption may depend not only on how high BTC can climb, but also on the financial opportunities created around the asset itself.

First, the annualized three-month CME Bitcoin futures basis would need to average more than two percentage points above three-month Treasury bill yields.

Second, open-interest-weighted Bitcoin funding rates would need to maintain a similar advantage.

The bank considers its forecast invalidated if either measure remains below Treasury bill yields for two consecutive quarters.

For Bitcoin investors, the broader significance extends beyond the potential returns of a single trading strategy.

An expanding derivatives market could improve liquidity, attract additional institutional participants, and support Bitcoin’s integration into traditional financial portfolios.

If these developments continue, Bitcoin’s next stage of institutional adoption may depend not only on how high BTC can climb, but also on the financial opportunities created around the asset itself.

title: Fourth Circuit Affirms Maryland’s Authority to Regulate Kalshi Prediction Markets
description:
A U.S. appellate court is upholding Maryland's right to enforce its sports wagering laws against Kalshi, marking another win for state oversight over federal preemption claims.
The post Fourth Circuit Affirms Maryland’s Authority to Regulate Kalshi Prediction Markets appeared first on The Daily Hodl.
fullContent:
A U.S. appellate court is affirming Maryland’s authority to enforce its sports wagering laws against the prediction market platform Kalshi.

The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit says the Commodity Exchange Act does not clearly preempt the state’s gaming laws even for event contracts on a CFTC-regulated designated contract market.

Judge Gregory concurring emphasizes that the regulation of gambling has long been a matter of traditional state police power.

“Because the regulation of gambling has long been a matter of traditional state police power, I would not infer that Congress displaced Maryland’s concurrent authority absent a clear expression of its intent to do so.”

The decision rejects Kalshi’s preemption arguments and finds no impossibility or obstacle to federal objectives.

Maryland Attorney General Anthony G. Brown says the ruling requires Kalshi to meet the same consumer protection standards as every other sportsbook serving Maryland residents.

“When betting platforms operate outside State oversight, Marylanders lose the protections that keep gambling fair and safe.”

“Today’s ruling means Kalshi must meet the same consumer protection standards as every other sportsbook serving Maryland residents.”

The per curiam opinion in case No. 25-1892 was decided November 18, 2026, after arguments on May 7, 2026.

description:

The post Bitcoin Nears $62,862 Mining Cost: Will BTC Price Hold Above This Level or Break Below It? appeared first on 99Bitcoins.
fullContent:
CryptoQuant founder Ki Young Ju said Noted that Bitcoin (BTC USD) has fallen to the price it costs to mine one Bitcoin. His chart, built from MARA Holdings’ filings, puts the miner’s average cost at $62,862 per coin in the third quarter. Bitcoin dipped to $62,063 on Wednesday and trades near $63,900 on Thursday.

“A break below could pressure public miners and their institutional backers,” Ki wrote on X. Below that price, a miner spends more to produce a coin than the coin is worth.

We checked how that line held up before. Bitcoin closed below $62,862 on 18 days since January 2025, all between June and August of this year. Each time, it was back above the line within a month.

This time, though, two forces push the other way: MARA is selling its Bitcoin, and ETF investors are pulling money out.

BTC USD Below Mining Cost: What Happened the Last Six Times

We compared Binance’s daily BTC USD closes since January 2025 with the $62,862 line. Bitcoin dropped below it in six separate stretches, all this summer.

  • Short dips: five of the six stretches lasted one or two days, in early June, July and on August 1.
  • The long one: from June 23 to July 3, Bitcoin closed below cost 11 days in a row. It hit $57,800 on July 1, its lowest price of the past year.
  • The recovery: 30 days after each stretch ended, Bitcoin was back above the line, but only by 1% to 3% in five cases. The exception was August 1, which was followed by a 25% rally to over $78,000.

So the mining cost has acted as a floor, but a soft one. It stopped the falls without starting a rally, until August.

The cost line also moves. MARA’s cost was close to $60,000 in the second quarter, so this summer’s dips were tested against a slightly lower bar than today’s.

DISCOVER: Bitcoin Price Crashes to $62K: Did Mara’s $1B BTC Sale Cause It?

MARA Is Selling, and ETF Investors Are Leaving

Two groups that usually support the price are selling instead.

  • MARA: the largest listed miner sold 13,597 BTC for about $1.1 billion over six weeks, at an average of about $81,000, roughly 29% above its own mining cost. It said it would keep selling to fund AI data centers. At today’s price, that margin has shrunk to about 2%.
  • Spot Bitcoin ETFs: these funds, which hold the coin itself, lost a net $239.9 million on Monday, November 17, with BlackRock’s IBIT accounting for $209.5 million. That came a day after IBIT’s first inflow in 11 sessions. Early figures point to another $306 million out on Tuesday.

The miners aren’t giving up, though. The network’s hashrate, the total computing power securing Bitcoin, averaged about 1,015 exahashes per second over the past 30 days. That’s 9% below its November 2025 peak but 13% above its August low. Miners are still adding machines, a sign they expect higher prices later.

DISCOVER: 20+ Next Crypto to Explode in 2026

BTC USD Price Analysis: The Mining Cost and $62,300 Sit Together

On the daily chart, BTC USD trades at $63,879. That is below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $75,252, and its 200-day EMA at $75,625.

  • Support: $62,300, just below the $62,862 mining cost. Bitcoin bounced near it on Sunday and Wednesday, after it also held in February, June, July and August. Below it, $57,800, the July low.
  • Resistance: $65,500, a level Bitcoin bounced from in early 2026 and was turned back from in June, July and August. Above that, $74,300.

BTCUSDT 1D chart. Source: TradingView

Path What has to happen Next stop
Bullish A daily close above $65,500 as ETF outflows stop $74,300, the March-September level
Sideways Price holds between $62,300 and $65,500 A range near the mining cost
Bearish A daily close below $62,300 and the mining cost $57,800, the July low

BTC USD has climbed back above the mining cost after all six dips this year. This time, miners are sellers and ETF money is leaving, so another recovery needs buyers to show up, not just sellers to stop.

title: HYPE Price Escapes One Trap, Walks Into Another
description:
Key Takeaways HYPE has left its late-October downtrend channel Two key resistance levels overlap near $70 Momentum still leans toward […]
The post HYPE Price Escapes One Trap, Walks Into Another appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Key Takeaways

  • HYPE has left its late-October downtrend channel
  • Two key resistance levels overlap near $70
  • Momentum still leans toward sellers
  • Team token unlocks begin November 29

The slide has hit a token that public companies have been accumulating: Hyperliquid Strategies (Nasdaq: PURR) reported spending $785 million on 9.1 million HYPE between July and September, lifting its treasury to 38.5 million tokens.

How HYPE Got Here

HYPE’s decline began in late October and followed a steep descending channel, a downward-sloping corridor formed by two parallel lines that contained almost every daily candle for the next three weeks. The heaviest trading volume of the period came at the start of that slide and again in mid-November, when sellers were most active.

The mid-November leg did the most damage. It pushed HYPE below its 200-day simple moving average (SMA), the average closing price of the past 200 days and a line many traders treat as the boundary between a healthy and a weakening trend. Until then, HYPE had stayed above that average for months. The same sell-off dragged the 14-day Relative Strength Index (RSI), a momentum gauge running from 0 to 100, down toward the 30 mark that traders read as oversold.

The Rebound So Far

Since that low, HYPE has climbed out of the channel. On the daily chart it trades around $69, above the corridor’s upper line, which shows sellers can no longer push the price down at the pace they managed earlier in the month.

The bounce has been cautious, though. RSI has recovered to about 38, only slightly above its signal line near 37 and still well short of the 50 mark associated with buyers taking control.

Why the Rally Stalls Just Below $70

Traders often map pullbacks with Fibonacci retracement levels, horizontal lines drawn at set percentages between a major low and high. Measured from HYPE’s late-July swing low to the spike high near $100 on this chart, the 0.618 retracement, one of the most closely watched, sits close to $70.

The 200-day SMA also runs at about $70, within a fraction of a dollar of that Fibonacci level. Before mid-November, this zone acted as a floor under HYPE. Now price is testing it from below, the position in which old support often turns into resistance. The last few sessions show that contest: one candle’s high poked above the zone, the next closed back near $67, and today’s session bounced from a low around $66.

What the Next Daily Close Would Signal

A single intraday spike in either direction says little. A daily close on either side of the $70 zone carries more weight.

If buyers break through

A decisive daily close above $70 would put HYPE back over both the 0.618 level and the 200-day SMA. If the zone then holds as support on a retest, the channel escape would become a reversal setup, with room opening toward the 0.5 Fibonacci level around $75.

If sellers hold the line

A push into the $70 zone followed by a close back below it would confirm the area has flipped to resistance. HYPE would then risk sliding back toward or inside the channel, with the 0.786 Fibonacci level near $61 in view, an area the mid-November low briefly dipped under.

Bigger Hurdles Further Up

Even a clean break above $70 leaves heavier resistance overhead. The 50-day SMA has been falling since early November and now sits just under the 100-day SMA, with both near $80 on the live candle. A daily close at those readings would confirm that the faster average has crossed below the slower one, a shift traders read as medium-term weakness.

The supply calendar adds another factor. FalconX research notes that HYPE’s first team token unlocks begin on November 29, bringing newly released tokens to market while price is still working through these levels.

fullContent:
After a much anticipated retail step, HSBC opened an HSBC RedCoin tokenised fund path for Hong Kong clients. Eligible customers can spend HSBC RedCoin in the HSBC HK App. They buy Class SD units of HSBC Global Money Funds – Hong Kong Dollar. Interestingly, the offer lands while RedCoin still sits early on PayMe rails and bank apps.

HSBC RedCoin Tokenised Fund Draws Orders Despite Token Rails

HSBC Global Asset Management set the Class SD public launch date at 18 November 2026. According to the October 2026 product brochure, one token represents one Class SD unit. Ownership sits on a permissioned blockchain. Meanwhile, the mutual funds page lists tokenised funds as now available on the HSBC HK App. The same page sets the entry at HKD100, funded with RCHKD100. According to the Guide to Tokenised Funds, subscription and settlement use HSBC RedCoin. Class SD Units can only be subscribed and redeemed through Eligible Distributors. The manager appoints those distributors.

The fund itself launched on 1 March 1991. According to HSBC Asset Management, fund size was HKD 20,774 million as of 30 September 2026. That is about HK$20.8 billion in short-term HKD deposits and money market paper. Weighted average maturity was 32 days on that date. Class SD carries a 0.30% management fee. Fitch rates the fund AAAmmf. Dividends declared on each business day reinvest into Class SD the same day. Cash dividend payouts are not available on that class. Capital preservation is not guaranteed. According to the firm, Class SD is a new share class on the same fund, not a new fund. It keeps the same underlying money market exposure as the older share classes. Dealing is daily on every dealing day. Switching out of the tokenised class is not permitted.

Meanwhile, RedCoin (RCHKD) is the licensed HKD stablecoin HSBC put on PayMe on 23 October 2026, after an early user ramp. The launch note said a tokenised money market share class would follow on the HSBC HK App. That rail is now live for the Class SD window. The brochure says Eligible Distributors must be SFC-licensed for dealing in securities or virtual asset trading. Tokenisation adds blockchain, custody, and distributor risks. Those sit beside ordinary money market risk. According to HSBC, buying units is not placing a bank deposit. The units are not under Hong Kong Monetary Authority deposit supervision. After a much anticipated wait, eligible Hong Kong clients can now clear a HKD money market order with RedCoin inside the banking app.

The post PDAX Lets Stablecoins Fund Philippine Retail Dollar Bonds appeared first on Live Bitcoin News.
fullContent:
After a much anticipated Retail Dollar Bonds Tranche 3 window, Philippine Digital Asset Exchange opened a PDAX stablecoin Philippine bonds funding path. Eligible USD stablecoins can fund those bond orders on the live public offer. Interestingly, the window lands while Manila still seeks at least $200 million from three-year onshore dollar notes due 2029.

PDAX Stablecoin Philippine Bonds Draw Orders Despite Friction

The Bureau of the Treasury set the public offer from November 19 to November 24. The issue date is November 27. According to The Philippine Star, citing the Treasury notice of offering, the minimum purchase is $200. The ceiling per order is the dollar equivalent of P500,000. Meanwhile, the final coupon is set through a Dutch auction among Government Securities Eligible Dealers. According to the same report, GCash GBonds and bank channels also take orders beside PDAX.

PDAX users fund the RDB3/USD pair after they hold enough USD. According to PDAX support, eligible USD stablecoins convert to USD in the FX tab at the live rate during set periods. According to Solana, the tokens accepted on the Solana network for this path include PYUSD, USDG, and USDPT. PHP cash-in and direct USD deposits also create USD. Meanwhile, PDAX Securities acts as the broker-dealer. Holdings sit in the investor's National Registry of Scripless Securities account.

PDAX is a Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas-supervised exchange that already sells Philippine government bonds in its app. Bank branches still take dollar retail orders. PDAX routes the same BTr paper through an in-app FX* balance that can start as a stablecoin. According to founder and CEO Nichel Gaba, Filipinos can buy the bonds through the PDAX app from $200. He said they do not need deep wealth or a private banker to reach that dollar paper.

The Offer Terms on the Table

Interestingly, the stablecoin conversion is not an open-ended tap. According to PDAX support, that option runs only in specified periods, and the live pairs sit in the app. Meanwhile, the Treasury can close the offer early or adjust the window. The bonds pay interest in USD on a quarterly schedule after issuance. Principal returns in USD at maturity. PDAX said it charges no primary-offer fees on the RDB 3 window. According to The Philippine Star, this is the third Retail Dollar Bond sale. The prior RDB 2 raise brought in $1.26 billion in October 2023. The maiden sale raised $1.6 billion in 2021. After a much anticipated wait, that stablecoin funding door now clears into the same sovereign paper.

title: OmenX announces $2 million in funding from Informed Ventures and launches on-demand 30-second Bitcoin predictions
description: The Base-native leveraged prediction market platform expands its offering across crypto, global financial assets, sports and esports. Toronto, November 19, 2026 – OmenX, a Base-native leveraged prediction market platform, today announced $2 million in funding from Informed Ventures alongside the launch of its on-demand, 30-second Bitcoin price prediction product. The new product lets users predict whether Bitcoin’s price will rise or fall over the next 30 seconds, with each trade starting its own prediction window. A position opened at 10:00:12 runs until 10:00:42. Users can act when their view forms, with a full 30-second horizon, rather than adapting to the remaining time in a shared market round. Featuring zero-slippage execution and rapid settlement, the product extends the familiar five- and fifteen-minute crypto prediction format to a shorter, individually timed experience. It adds to OmenX’s intraday offering, which spans prediction horizons from 30 seconds to 24 hours, depending on the market. Beyond crypto, OmenX offers directional prediction markets linked to more than 100 global assets, including U.S. equities, futures, ETFs and indices. Its event markets also cover live sports and esports, with sports coverage spanning major football leagues, basketball, American football, ice hockey, baseball and UFC. Leverage has been central to OmenX’s platform from the outset, allowing traders to amplify their exposure on supported event markets. The latest launch builds on that foundation while advancing a broader goal: making prediction markets a practical financial tool for retail users. OmenX organizes the trading decision around a defined question: will an asset’s price be higher or lower at the end of a specified period? Users can express a directional view without purchasing the underlying asset, targeting an exact closing price or constructing an options position that requires decisions about strikes, implied volatility and time decay. “Leverage has been part of OmenX from the start, but our ambition goes beyond adding leverage to prediction markets,” said James, founder and CEO of OmenX. “We want to make global markets easier to participate in. A trader should be able to take a view on Bitcoin, a stock or a sporting event and express it through a clear contract and a timeframe that fits their judgment.” The platform’s emphasis on short, recurring markets provides faster feedback on trading decisions and can reduce the time capital remains committed to individual outcomes. OmenX plans to expand its coverage of traditional and crypto assets while deepening the trading experience across supported markets. title: GTA 6 Flu Is Here: The Impact on Crypto Markets
description:
GTA 6 is taking over workplaces and social media as crypto markets go quiet. Could the gaming frenzy pull retail traders away from crypto?
The post GTA 6 Flu Is Here: The Impact on Crypto Markets appeared first on Cryptonews.
fullContent:
GTA 6 has finally arrived, and millions of gamers are putting everything else on hold, including crypto portfolios.

After 13 years of waiting, Rockstar’s blockbuster release is already disrupting workplaces, dominating social media, and pulling gamers away from their usual routines. Even our newsroom is feeling the impact, with maybe 30% of employees taking days off.

Could GTA 6 be stealing retail’s attention just as digital asset markets struggle to bring individual investors back?

GTA 6 Could Be Taking Retail Attention Away From Crypto

The scale of the launch is hard to ignore. GTA 6 sold around 17.1 million copies before its worldwide release. The game also carries expectations of $1.85 billion in revenue during its first three days.

Workers are making room for it, too. UKG data covering two million US employees showed time-off requests for launch day running about 20% above normal levels. A separate Zety survey found 22% of Gen Z workers planned around the release.

That is a sizeable chunk of the demographic that crypto platforms have spent years trying to attract. The overlap of both gaming and crypto competes for online attention, particularly among younger audiences who spend hours on streaming platforms, social media and digital communities.

For us, checking Bitcoin prices, chasing the latest meme coin and following market-moving posts can easily become part of the daily routine. But GTA 6 offers something considerably more entertaining than watching another sideways trading session.

The launch is also driving enormous engagement across YouTube and Reddit. Sensor Tower estimates point to more than 50 million additional visits to food delivery and restaurant apps in the US over 30 days.

Crypto’s social media ecosystem could find itself competing for a much smaller share of that attention.

Discover: The Best Token Presales

Crypto Retail Activity Was Already Losing Steam

There is another reason the timing is interesting. Retail crypto trading has been weakening even as the broader market has attracted fresh capital.

Data reported from eToro clients placed 62% fewer crypto trades in October than a year earlier. Robinhood’s crypto trading volume also fell 48% year over year in the third quarter, while Coinbase consumer spot volume dropped 59%.

The figures show that rising market valuations have not translated into the same level of retail trading activity seen during previous cycles.

This leaves crypto exposed to competition for speculative attention. Institutional investors can continue trading through market cycles, but retail often depends on excitement, momentum, and whatever narrative is dominating the internet.

But GTA 6 has all three. The game could temporarily pull casual traders away from exchanges, particularly those who spend their evenings chasing small-cap tokens and following crypto KOLs. Meme coins could be especially vulnerable if their usual audience spends the next several days exploring Vice City instead.

There is also an ironic possibility that GTA 6 could create fresh opportunities for crypto speculation. Gaming-themed tokens and GTA-related meme coins could attract traders looking to profit from the launch itself.

Bitcoin does not need gamers watching charts every minute to keep trading. But an industry built around speculation, online communities, and retail enthusiasm cannot afford to ignore where that attention goes.

fullContent:
A 22-year-old Miami man is accused of making 32 fraudulent wire transfers worth more than $600,000.

Donnell Collier Jr. allegedly carried out an account-takeover scheme tied to a nationwide bank fraud crackdown, according to federal court records, reports CBS12.

Collier faces charges of wire fraud conspiracy, wire fraud and bank fraud.

If convicted, he could face up to 80 years in federal prison.

His arrest was one of five in Florida tied to fraud schemes linked to more than $54 million in losses at over 65 financial institutions nationwide.

The operation involved FBI offices in Miami, Nashville, New York, Columbia, Houston and Omaha.

Four suspects were arrested in South Florida while a fifth South Florida resident was arrested in Central Florida.

Brioden Jean and Derek Val Pierre-Paul are charged in Tennessee with wire fraud conspiracy and two counts of wire fraud.

Kevin Lopez and John Sardinas are charged in Iowa with money laundering conspiracy and four counts of money laundering.

title: Ripple CEO Predicts Utility-Driven Crypto Will Win — Could XRP Be The Biggest Beneficiary?
description: Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse believes the cryptocurrency market is approaching a major turning point, where real-world utility could become more important than speculation. His latest comments come as institutional XRP infrastructure continues expanding, raising fresh questions about whether XRP could benefit from a more utility-driven market. Speaking with Bloomberg’s Haslinda Amin at Singapore FinTech Festival […]
fullContent:
Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse believes the cryptocurrency market is approaching a major turning point, where real-world utility could become more important than speculation. His latest comments come as institutional XRP infrastructure continues expanding, raising fresh questions about whether XRP could benefit from a more utility-driven market.

Speaking with Bloomberg’s Haslinda Amin at Singapore FinTech Festival 2026 on November 19, Garlinghouse predicted that cryptocurrencies would increasingly diverge in performance as investors begin distinguishing between assets supported by genuine demand and those relying primarily on speculation.

The comments arrive during a challenging period for digital assets, with XRP struggling to reflect Ripple’s growing institutional presence in its market valuation.

However, a separate announcement involving the XRP Ledger could strengthen the argument that real-world adoption is becoming an increasingly important part of XRP’s long-term investment narrative.

Ripple CEO Predicts A Major Change In Crypto Markets

During his Bloomberg interview, Garlinghouse explained that cryptocurrencies have historically moved together, particularly during periods of market volatility.

He believes that relationship could gradually change.

According to the Ripple executive, assets with genuine financial applications and sustained demand may begin outperforming tokens whose value depends primarily on speculative trading.

Garlinghouse also acknowledged that 2026 has been difficult for the cryptocurrency market, pointing to capital moving toward major technology IPOs as one possible explanation for recent selling pressure.

Nevertheless, his longer-term outlook remains constructive.

The CEO argued that blockchain technology can improve financial transactions through faster and cheaper settlement, with applications extending beyond payments into tokenization, insurance, and other financial services.

For XRP, the distinction between utility and speculation is particularly important.

Although XRP was developed to facilitate efficient value transfers, its market performance remains heavily influenced by broader cryptocurrency sentiment.

The challenge is determining whether growing institutional use of Ripple’s infrastructure will eventually generate enough XRP-specific demand to influence the token’s valuation.

XRP Ledger Reaches An Important Institutional Milestone

Garlinghouse’s comments coincide with a significant development involving the XRP Ledger.

On November 18, the XRP Ledger Foundation announced that it had completed a self-attestation against the ten principles of the Global Layer One (GL1) Market Infrastructure Toolkit.

Blockchain security firm CertiK independently reviewed the Foundation’s responses under the framework’s Architecture and Resiliency principles.

The development makes XRPL the first public, permissionless Layer 1 blockchain to complete this particular independently verified assessment.

The framework covers areas including governance, settlement finality, operational resilience, cybersecurity, and institutional access.

These considerations are particularly important for banks and asset managers evaluating blockchain infrastructure for tokenized financial assets.

However, the assessment does not constitute regulatory approval, certification, or endorsement by GL1.

Ripple highlighted the milestone through its official X account, emphasizing the importance of infrastructure that financial institutions can evaluate against established standards.

The announcement reinforces the broader institutional narrative surrounding XRP Ledger, although independent verification of specific technical controls does not automatically translate into additional XRP demand.

Why Institutional Adoption Could Become XRP’s Biggest Advantage

Ripple’s growing institutional network provides another important element of Garlinghouse’s argument.

The company recently announced expanded relationships with major financial institutions, including BNY and Robinhood, involving payments, stablecoins, treasury services, and other blockchain-based financial applications.

Meanwhile, Bitcoinist recently reported that Aviva Investors expanded tokenization on XRPL, introducing a tokenized share class of its Sterling Liquidity Fund.

These developments demonstrate how traditional financial institutions are increasingly exploring blockchain infrastructure for applications beyond cryptocurrency trading.

Yet an important distinction remains.

Ripple’s corporate expansion, XRP Ledger activity, and demand for XRP are related but separate measures.

A company using Ripple’s software or the RLUSD stablecoin does not necessarily need to acquire large quantities of XRP.

For institutional adoption to support XRP’s market valuation, investors would need evidence of increasing XRP-based settlement activity, liquidity demand, and broader network participation.

Could XRP Benefit From A Utility-Driven Crypto Market?

Garlinghouse’s prediction introduces an interesting possibility for XRP’s long-term investment outlook.

If investors increasingly prioritize digital assets with established financial applications, XRP could benefit from its role as a bridge asset and its connection to an expanding blockchain ecosystem.

Ripple has repeatedly emphasized that XRP remains central to its strategy, even as the company develops stablecoin infrastructure.

However, stablecoins also introduce competition in certain payment scenarios.

Dollar-denominated assets such as RLUSD can provide an alternative when financial institutions want to transfer stable value rather than use a volatile bridge asset.

The opportunity for XRP may therefore depend on whether its liquidity and settlement capabilities provide measurable advantages in specific cross-border payment corridors.

This is particularly relevant as financial institutions explore tokenized deposits, stablecoins, and other digital settlement mechanisms.

XRP Price Analysis: Can Utility Support A Recovery?

Despite Ripple’s expanding institutional relationships, XRP has faced significant selling pressure during November.

Recent market analysis highlighted the importance of the psychological $1 level, with the token struggling to establish a sustained recovery.

From a technical perspective, reclaiming $1 could improve short-term sentiment, but a convincing reversal would require stronger confirmation.

Investors should monitor whether XRP can establish higher lows, improve trading volume, and eventually reclaim its 50-day and 200-day moving averages.

A sustained recovery above these indicators would suggest that buying pressure is strengthening.

Conversely, continued weakness below major moving averages would indicate that broader market conditions remain an obstacle.

As Bitcoinist previously examined in its coverage of institutional XRP liquidity, expanding financial infrastructure may create opportunities for the ecosystem without guaranteeing an immediate increase in token prices.

For now, the most constructive scenario would involve improving technical momentum alongside measurable growth in XRP-based transactions.

What Comes Next For Ripple And XRP?

Garlinghouse’s latest comments highlight an important question facing the cryptocurrency industry: will investors continue valuing digital assets primarily through speculation, or will measurable adoption become increasingly important?

Ripple’s expanding institutional relationships and the XRP Ledger’s latest infrastructure assessment suggest that the company is positioning itself for a more utility-focused market.

However, the long-term implications for XRP will depend on actual transaction demand, liquidity, and the extent to which institutional applications require the token.

If cryptocurrencies begin diverging according to their real-world usefulness, XRP’s ability to convert institutional adoption into sustained token demand could become one of the market’s most important developments to watch.

title: Binance Hacker Moves Another $248M of Ethereum as the Exchange Pockets $6.5B Court Order
description:
Binance hacker has moved another $248 million in Ethereum as the exchange secures a major legal victory against the attackers. Blockchain tracker Lookonchain reported that 137,602 ETH moved across multiple wallets today, extending a three-day distribution spree. The latest transfers bring the total moved since November 17 to nearly 291,000 ETH, worth more than $500..
The post Binance Hacker Moves Another $248M of Ethereum as the Exchange Pockets $6.5B Court Order appeared first on 99Bitcoins.
fullContent:
Binance hacker has moved another $248 million in Ethereum as the exchange secures a major legal victory against the attackers. Blockchain tracker Lookonchain reported that 137,602 ETH moved across multiple wallets today, extending a three-day distribution spree.

The latest transfers bring the total moved since November 17 to nearly 291,000 ETH, worth more than $500 million. The activity comes as Binance pursues a worldwide freezing order from Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) courts.

The court order covers $6.5 billion in stolen assets and targets unidentified individuals behind the October 29 breach. Binance now has a legal route to pursue frozen funds, but the attackers are still shifting hundreds of millions through Ethereum wallets.

Market Cap

Binance Pockets $6.5B Court Order as Hackers Keep Moving Funds

Binance secured the worldwide freezing injunction yesterday, giving its recovery operation a significant legal boost. The ADGM Court also issued separate orders covering specific stolen assets held by third parties.

Eighteen crypto companies must maintain existing freezes and cannot lend, swap, or mix the affected tokens. They include Circle and World Liberty Financial, neither of which faces allegations of wrongdoing.

JUST IN: Binance says it secured a court order in Abu Dhabi to help recover crypto frozen after last month’s $6.3 billion hack, per Reuters.

Binance previously said third parties had frozen or intercepted about $2.85 billion, roughly 45% of the stolen crypto.

The court order… pic.twitter.com/Dx4wI7jlI5

— Coin Bureau (@coinbureau) November 18, 2026

Binance’s lawyers have identified 26,000 wallet addresses holding stolen assets. The exchange says around $2.85 billion has already been frozen or intercepted, or 45% of the original theft.

Tether has separately frozen $1.5 billion linked to the attack. Although the stablecoin issuer was not named in the court order, it is working directly with Binance on returning the funds.

The legal offensive comes as Binance tries to recover assets that investigators have traced across multiple blockchains. The exchange has already reimbursed affected customers and covered the financial loss. This leaves billions worth of crypto still moving through wallets controlled by the attackers.

DISCOVER: 15+ Best Crypto IPO to Watch in 2026

Binance Hacker’s Ethereum Transfers Reach Nearly 291,000 ETH in Three Days

The movement involved 12 transfers to 12 separate recipient addresses. Eleven transactions carried 12,000 ETH each, while the final transfer contained 5,602 ETH.

The transfers followed two large movements earlier this week. Hack-linked wallets redistributed 74,880 ETH on November 17 and another 78,415 ETH on November 18.

Combined, the three batches account for approximately 290,898 ETH. The latest $248.23 million transfer represents the largest daily movement identified during this period.

The Binance hacker has moved another 137,602 $ETH ($248.23M) for laundering.https://t.co/jKWvcOSJCB pic.twitter.com/ZcIoZLlAhA

— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) November 19, 2026

The FBI attributed the October 29 theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor operation. Its October 31 alert identified Ethereum addresses operated by or closely connected to the attackers.

Some of the earlier transfers have already entered Bitcoin. Blockchain intelligence firm Elliptic identified 2,100 ETH converted into BTC from the November 17 movement. Much of that Bitcoin subsequently entered CoinJoin transactions, which complicate transaction tracing.

The latest batch consisted of wallet-to-wallet transfers. Splitting the funds across new addresses gives investigators more wallets to track as the laundering operation progresses.

Binance’s legal team is building a constantly updated list of suspect addresses. The court orders can be served through blockchain transactions, allowing exchanges and other service providers to identify affected funds.

The next major milestone arrives on December 1, when the ADGM Court will consider if the proprietary injunction should continue. Meanwhile, every new transfer gives investigators another opportunity to identify where the stolen Ethereum goes.

title: PayPal’s Stablecoin Users Can Disappear Inside Custody
description:
Key Takeaways Only 2% of PYUSD sits in small wallets Paxos custody holds $789M for customers and partners Lending and […]
The post PayPal’s Stablecoin Users Can Disappear Inside Custody appeared first on Coindoo.
fullContent:
Key Takeaways

  • Only 2% of PYUSD sits in small wallets
  • Paxos custody holds $789M for customers and partners
  • Lending and yield products account for 28%
  • Checkout payments settle to merchants in dollars

Bitquery’s holder investigation, published November 19 with balances verified a day earlier, traced $2.33 billion of the token’s roughly $2.46 billion supply across Ethereum, Solana, Arbitrum and Polygon.

Where the $2.33 Billion Sits

Bitquery sorted every measured balance into nine categories. The one closest to everyday users, unlabelled wallets holding less than $1 million, accounts for $49 million.

Measured PYUSD supply by holder type

Paxos custody $789M · 34%
DeFi lending $493M · 21%
Unlabelled wallets, $1M+$313M · 13%
Trading firms $268M · 12%
Yield products $159M · 7%
Exchanges $140M · 6%
Trading pools $83M · 4%
Ordinary wallets, under $1M$49M · 2%
Bridges $35M · 1%

Source: Bitquery. Balances verified November 18, 2026, on Ethereum, Solana, Arbitrum and Polygon. Shares are rounded.

The $1 million cutoff decides a great deal. An unlabelled wallet holding $1.2 million falls into a bucket more than six times larger than the ordinary category, while a $900,000 wallet run by a small fund still counts as ordinary. Bitquery assigns labels from known addresses and from how wallets transact with each other, so its categories describe on-chain behaviour rather than verified identities.

The snapshot also runs on two clocks. Ethereum balances were read at midnight UTC on November 18 and Solana balances at 16:21 UTC, so tokens bridged between those chains in the gap could be counted twice or missed. The shares are close approximations of a supply that kept moving during the measurement.

One Custody Bucket, Many Possible Owners

Paxos Trust Company issues PYUSD for PayPal, and its custody wallets hold $789 million, the largest single category. Bitquery says those wallets keep coins for Paxos’s customers and partners, including people who hold PYUSD inside an app, and that the chain does not show which coins belong to PayPal or Venmo users.

PayPal’s own setup explains the blind spot. Its US cryptocurrency terms say it combines customers’ crypto in omnibus accounts, meaning pooled accounts that hold assets for many customers at once, directly or through a service provider, and keeps a separate record of each customer’s interest. Under those terms, customers do not own specific tokens, and the PYUSD balance shown in the app is not tied to a particular blockchain.

Take a hypothetical pool of 1,000 customers holding 100 PYUSD each. The provider’s books show 1,000 owners and 100,000 tokens. On-chain, the same money could sit in a handful of addresses, and a holder chart would file all of it under custody.

Bitquery did find one trace of the people behind the pool. Over the past year, Paxos custody sent payments to 141,617 unlabelled Ethereum wallets, and 68% of those payments were under $100. Bitquery reads the pattern as users moving coins out of apps, while noting that the chain does not show who requested each transfer. One person can control several receiving wallets, so the number is no user count, but it shows small-ticket withdrawals leaving custody at scale.

Lending Protocols Hold 14 Times More Than Small Wallets

DeFi lending and yield products together hold 28% of measured supply. On Ethereum, Spark holds $304 million, Morpho $103 million and Maple $65 million. Bitquery says these protocols lend PYUSD out or use it to back other dollar tokens. On Arbitrum, a single protocol, USD.AI, holds roughly four in five of the coins on that chain.

Trading follows the same pattern. Bitquery found that 95% of Ethereum PYUSD trading over the past year was against USDS, the dollar token of the Sky ecosystem that includes Spark, and was concentrated in a few pools. The firm describes this as money moving between two DeFi systems and says buyers acquiring the coin to spend make up a small part of it.

A lending contract is another pooled holder. The address belongs to the protocol, while the economic interest belongs to depositors and borrowers the balance never names. The 28% shows where PYUSD earns a return, and the number of depositors behind it stays off the chart.

READ MORE:

Ant, DBS Use Blockchain Cash to Buy Tokenized Funds

Checkout Payments End in Dollars

Payments leave even fewer marks. Under PayPal’s Pay with Crypto terms, a shopper at an eligible merchant is connected to Mesh Connect, a third-party provider that acts on the shopper’s instructions. Mesh moves PYUSD from the shopper’s wallet to PayPal, first converting another supported cryptocurrency into PYUSD if needed.

After risk and compliance checks, PayPal converts the PYUSD to US dollars at $1.00 per token and credits the merchant’s business balance, net of fees. Refunds run the other way: the merchant enters the amount in dollars, and PayPal sends PYUSD back to the shopper’s wallet.

The merchant never holds the token, so a snapshot taken after the sale shows no PYUSD on the business side. A company that keeps stablecoins as working capital would appear on-chain, and one using PayPal’s checkout would not, even if both serve the same customers. The terms set out the mechanics but give no figure for how often the route is used. Coindoo’s guide to how crypto payments reach merchants covers the wider settlement process.

What a User Count Would Require

PYUSD has been available in 70 markets since PayPal’s March expansion, which describes how far the product reaches. Measuring how many people use it takes records that only PayPal and Paxos hold.

Who holds it?

Deduplicated account records, with the apps and regions they cover stated

Who pays with it?

Completed checkouts, separated from withdrawals and wallet-to-wallet transfers

Who comes back?

Repeat-payment cohorts tracked over fixed periods

Even provider numbers would need definitions. An account with a few cents left over is not an active payer, and someone who pays monthly may hold nothing on the day of a snapshot. Counting both as users would blur the behaviour an adoption figure is meant to capture.

On the evidence available, the 2% figure supports neither a weak nor a strong reading of PayPal’s retail audience. Small wallets hold little, yet custody has paid out to more than 140,000 wallets in mostly small amounts, and checkout leaves no balance behind. Paxos already publishes reserve reports and attestations on what backs PYUSD. Comparable figures on funded accounts and completed payments would answer the question a wallet chart cannot.

fullContent:
Solana (SOL)
24h7d30d1yAll time

Solana’s tokenized stock market has reached $1.22 billion in circulating value, nearly doubling in less than a month as demand for blockchain-based equities accelerates.

Growth has been driven by platforms including Ondo Finance, xStocks and Backpack Securities, which are bringing exposure to major US companies onto Solana. Apple, Nvidia, Tesla and other household names are increasingly appearing in crypto wallets and decentralized trading platforms.

The expansion is also attracting traditional financial infrastructure. The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC) plans to connect its tokenization service to Solana in 2027, potentially opening another route for established securities to enter blockchain markets.

Discover: The Best Token Presales

Ondo and xStocks Push Solana Tokenized Equities Beyond $1 Billion

Ondo Finance has become one of the biggest contributors to Solana’s tokenized stock market. The platform brought more than 200 tokenized US stocks and ETFs to the network in January, covering companies such as Nvidia, Apple, and Meta.

Its expansion has continued through additional trading and wallet integrations. According to the Solana Foundation’s October ecosystem report, Ondo’s tokenized assets on Solana surpassed $500 million.

Meanwhile, xStocks has accumulated $7.5 billion in trading volume on Solana, while Backpack Securities has processed more than $6 billion in tokenized asset trading volume.

Securitize is also expanding its presence. The company added 13 US equities to its Solana-based offering on November 2, bringing its total catalogue to 25 stocks. Its products include shares in Exxon Mobil, Disney, Salesforce, and GameStop. Unlike purely synthetic products, Securitize says its tokens are backed one-to-one by underlying shares and provide security entitlements with applicable economic and ownership rights.

DTCC Brings Solana Closer to Traditional Financial Markets

The biggest institutional development came on November 12, when DTCC announced plans to connect its Tokenization Service to Solana during the second half of 2027. The integration would allow eligible securities held through its Depository Trust Company subsidiary to become available in tokenized form on Solana.

DTCC is one of the most important pieces of infrastructure in US financial markets. Its subsidiaries processed $4.7 quadrillion in securities transactions during 2025, while its depository provided custody and asset servicing for $114 trillion in securities.

The initial tokenization service launched on October 28, with support for Canton Network and DTCC’s private Besu network. Solana will become another destination as the company expands its blockchain integrations.

Twenty financial institutions signed agreements to access the service at launch, including JPMorgan, Bank of America, Citi, Morgan Stanley and UBS. DTCC says tokenized securities distributed through its service will retain the ownership rights, investor protections and regulatory safeguards associated with traditionally held securities.

This gives Solana a potential connection to established securities infrastructure rather than relying exclusively on crypto-native issuers and trading platforms. But the integration is still planned for 2027.

As of now, the $1.22 billion milestone reflects a relatively small market compared with traditional equities. But the combination of expanding stock offerings, billions in cumulative trading activity, and growing institutional involvement suggests tokenization is becoming a more serious part of Solana’s financial ecosystem.

Bitcoin Hyper Eyes Solana Tokenized Stock Boom With Bitcoin Liquidity

Solana is attracting billions in tokenized stock trading, but Bitcoin Hyper is betting that the next opportunity lies in bringing Bitcoin liquidity into a faster, more flexible blockchain environment.

Bitcoin Hyper ($HYPER) is developing a Bitcoin Layer 2 powered by the Solana Virtual Machine (SVM). The architecture aims to combine Bitcoin’s enormous liquidity base with the speed and programmability associated with Solana.

Users will be able to bridge BTC into the Layer 2, where they can access faster transactions, decentralized exchanges, staking, and other DeFi applications. Its design also uses zero-knowledge proofs and periodic state commitments to Bitcoin for settlement.

That combination could open an interesting route for tokenized financial markets. Solana has already demonstrated demand for bringing traditional equities onchain. Bitcoin Hyper is targeting a different pool of capital: Bitcoin holders who want access to applications beyond simply holding BTC.

The project has already attracted more than $33 million during its presale, while its testnet infrastructure is taking shape. Its wallet, explorer, faucet, and testnet bridge are among the components being rolled out ahead of the next development phase.

The HYPER token currently costs just $0.0136, with presale staking offering an advertised 35% APY. That yield gives early participants another incentive to hold their tokens while the network develops. Bitcoin Hyper is using staking rewards to attract early participation before its wider ecosystem goes live.

The fundraising milestone also puts the project on a defined timeline. Bitcoin Hyper’s presale is scheduled to conclude on November 26, leaving buyers with a shrinking window before the next stage.
